## renv — package version locking
To lock exact package versions for reproducibility, run once from the R console
after all packages are installed and working:
```r
# renv::init()     # first time: initialise and snapshot
# renv::snapshot() # after adding/updating packages
# renv::restore()  # collaborators run this to install exact same versions
```
Do NOT run renv::init() mid-analysis — do it when the project is stable and
ready for GitHub. The renv.lock file should be committed to the repository.

## Functions
```{r functions, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# function to remove rows with n number of NA's
delete.na <- function(DF, n=0) {
  DF[rowSums(is.na(DF)) <= n,]
}

# Specify alpha as a percentage:
colorRampAlpha <- function(..., n, alpha) {
   colors <- colorRampPalette(...)(n)
   paste(colors, sprintf("%x", ceiling(255*alpha)), sep="")
}

```


## Universal variables
```{r define_universal}
stud_pat <- "RS_surface"

## All inputs, outputs, and plots live in the '2026 RS eDNA' folder.
dir         <- paste0(here::here("2026 RS eDNA"), "/")
export_file <- ""       # CSV exports → dir  (empty = same as dir)
## out_file not currently used; kept as placeholder for future summary exports
plot_file   <- "plots"  # plots subfolder: dir/plots/

# filtered sequence data (output of post-DADA2 Rmd)
dat_name <- paste0(stud_pat, "_filtered_data_all.csv")


## set some other universal variables
####  !!!! need to be in alphabetical order - tabs in sam_file should match these names too !!!!! also have "type"" column
primers <- c('18smini', "euka02")   # 18S_V9 and 18S_V7 only
n_primers <- length(primers)
## must be in alphabetical order

####  !!!! set minimum reads per sample to remove  !!!!!   ####
# min_reads_per_sample<- 1
# now use chunk below to determine

################### set file path and name of sample data

sam_file_path <- paste0(dir, "RS_surface_sample_data_all.xlsx")
```

## Set minimum reads
```{r set_mins_divs}

# fac includes -per sample     reads, mean hab reads ,rich, div

####      !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
#   !!!!!!!!! take a look at rare_mins, most in cores have very low     !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
####      !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
### get summary number of reads per sample (only true samples).. for rarefy
rare_mins<-dat %>%   # names(dat_filt_taxa_df)
  filter(type=="sample") %>% 
  dplyr::select(primer_taxassign_id, sample_id_u, reads) %>% 
  group_by(primer_taxassign_id,sample_id_u) %>% 
  summarise(sum_sample=sum(reads)) %>% 
  group_by(primer_taxassign_id) %>% 
  summarise(min_sample=min(sum_sample),upper_quant=quantile(sum_sample, probs=0.75),  low_quant=quantile(sum_sample, probs=0.25), seventyfivepercent_lower=0.75*low_quant, fiftypercent_lower=0.50*low_quant, one_third_lower=0.333*low_quant, low_10percent=quantile(sum_sample, probs=0.10), lower_wisker= low_quant -( (upper_quant-low_quant)*0.5 ) , median=median(sum_sample), mean=mean(sum_sample),num_samp=n(),samp_below_quant= length(sum_sample[sum_sample<low_quant]), samp_below_75= length(sum_sample[sum_sample<seventyfivepercent_lower]), samp_below_50= length(sum_sample[sum_sample<fiftypercent_lower]), samp_below66 = length(sum_sample[sum_sample < one_third_lower]) , samp_below_10p= length(sum_sample[sum_sample<low_10percent]), samp_below_wisk= length(sum_sample[sum_sample<lower_wisker]))
#   !!!!!!!!! take a look, most in cores have very low rare to 3000 remove any sample less than 1000
# Feb 2021, try to automate rarefy decision.....
#  seems like fair trade off between being too stringent for min. reads and removing samples with fewer reads than min ..
#   use lower quartile (75% of samples) for minimum for rarefaction and then remove 10% of samples with low reads.
##  this results in about 10% samples removed and 10% of samples have reads below rarefaction minumum.

##   !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
#   set min and remove_sample
#  min_num_rarefaction<-3000
#   sample_read_min<-1000
#  BETTER  !!!!!!    or set rare and min for each miseq run     # names(rare_mins)
min_reads_min<-rare_mins[,c(1,4,6)]
min_num_rarefaction<-as.vector(rare_mins$low_quant)
sample_read_min<-as.vector(rare_mins$fiftypercent_lower)

# The data-driven threshold (50% of Q1) gives 4713 (18smini) and 4851 (euka02).
# A fixed cutoff of 4500 is used instead: two borderline samples were excluded
# by the data-driven threshold despite one primer performing well (>24000 reads):
#   DC 2017 M D1 (Mangrove): euka02 = 4564 reads, 18smini = 32635 reads
#   DC 2017 S6   (Seagrass): 18smini = 4520 reads, euka02 = 24129 reads
# Both samples are just below the data-driven threshold for one primer only;
# the other primer has excellent coverage. A cutoff of 4500 recovers both
# without altering the status of any other sample.
min_reads_min <- min_reads_min %>%
  mutate(fiftypercent_lower = 4500)
```

## Tidy data

```{r tiding}

# make simple sample names  -- new names unique for all samples - not done before
sample_names_good <- dat %>%    #   names(dat)
  filter(!duplicated(sample_id_u))  %>% 
  select(sample_id_u) %>% 
  mutate(num=1:length(row.names(.)), sample_id_meta=paste("x_",num,sep="")) %>% 
  select(-num)


## tidy env data
## CSV has both non-near (grid-cell) and _near (nearest-cell) versions of each
## variable. Drop the non-near versions and rename _near to short working names.
## NOTE: the _near columns have a SPACE before the underscore in their names
## (e.g. "Present.Surface.Temperature.Mean _near") — backticks required.
## Use dplyr::rename() explicitly in case terra is ever loaded (it masks rename).
env <- env %>%   # names(env)
  select(
    -land_distance,
    -`Present.Surface.Temperature.Mean`,
    -`Present.Surface.Temperature.Range`,
    -`Present.Surface.Primary.productivity.Mean`,
    -`Present.Surface.Primary.productivity.Range`,
    -`Present.Surface.Salinity.Mean`,
    -`Present.Surface.Nitrate.Mean`,
    -`Present.Surface.Par.Mean`
  ) %>%
  dplyr::rename(
    sst_mean      = `Present.Surface.Temperature.Mean _near`,
    SST_range     = `Present.Surface.Temperature.Range _near`,
    pp_mean     = `Present.Surface.Primary.productivity.Mean _near`,
    pp_range    = `Present.Surface.Primary.productivity.Range _near`,
    salinity      = `Present.Surface.Salinity.Mean _near`,
    nitrate       = `Present.Surface.Nitrate.Mean _near`,
    PAR           = `Present.Surface.Par.Mean _near`,
    land_distance = land_distance_near
  )



###      tidy sequence data
 # unique(sample_age1$dating_type)
dat_all<- dat %>%   # names(dat)   names(dat_all)
  filter(reads>0) %>%

  ## strip XML artifact prefix from sample_id — the sequence CSV has
  ## 'xml:space="preserve">' (or double-quote-escaped variant) prepended to
  ## CCF sample IDs. Match everything up to and including the first '>',
  ## then trim whitespace to catch trailing spaces left after stripping.
  mutate(sample_id = stringr::str_trim(
    stringr::str_remove(sample_id, '^xml:space[^>]*>')
  )) %>%

  ## ── Strip numeric cluster suffix from lineage ─────────────────────────────
  ## The decon version of post_DADA2_filter_and_tidy.Rmd appends a DECIPHER
  ## cluster number as the final ;-delimited field (e.g. "...;Genus sp;-42").
  ## Check whether the last field is purely numeric (incl. optional leading "-")
  ## and remove it if so — otherwise leave the lineage unchanged.
  ## Must happen FIRST: different primers get different cluster IDs for the same
  ## taxon, so the suffix blocks correct collapsing across primers downstream.
  mutate(lineage = stringr::str_replace(lineage, ";-?\\d+$", "")) %>%

  mutate(type_3cat=forcats::fct_recode(type, "blank"="extraction blank", "blank" = "pcr blank", "mock" = "positive control")) %>%
  
  #mutate(ybp_cat=cut(ybp, breaks=c(-Inf,10,50,100,250,500, Inf),labels=c("<10","10-50","50-100","100-250","250-500",">500"))) %>%  

  #mutate(ybp_cat_blanks=if_else(is.na(ybp_cat), type_3cat  , ybp_cat )) %>% # bring blanks into age cat
    # unique(dat2$ybp_cat_blanks)
  mutate(percent_reads=reads/sample_sum_after_filt*100)  %>% 
  mutate(log_reads=log(reads+1), log_rare_reads=log(rare_reads+1), log_percent_reads=log(percent_reads+1) )  %>% 
    mutate(primer=forcats::fct_recode(primer, "18S_V7"="euka02", "18S_V9"="18smini","CO1"="co1", "Vert"="vert")) %>% # "18S_V4"="18s_stoeck"
  mutate(primer_name=factor(primer,levels=c("18S_V9","18S_V7","CO1","Vert","rbclmini"))) %>% # ,"18S_V4"

  ## get new/good sample names
  left_join(sample_names_good)

#    !!!!!!!!
#    !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!   limit  ??????????????    !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
# final filtering, make df with 18s
dat_all_filt <- dat_all %>%    
    filter(minboot==70) %>% 
   # filter(primer!="rbclmini") %>% 
   # filter(primer!="Vert") %>% 

  filter(grepl("18S", primer)) %>%   # "18S"  "18S_V9"
  mutate(primer=factor(primer)) %>%   # levels(x$primer)
  
  # remove reps
  filter(!grepl("rep", sample_id)) %>% 
  # only samples
  filter(type=="sample") %>% 

    ## !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
    ## remove samples with minimal reads — fixed cutoff of 4500 reads
    ## (data-driven 50% Q1 gives 4713 / 4851; lowered to recover two
    ##  borderline samples with one strong and one near-threshold primer)
  left_join(min_reads_min)  %>%  # names(min_reads_min)
  filter(sample_sum_after_filt > fiftypercent_lower) %>%
  select(-low_quant, -fiftypercent_lower) %>%

    ## !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
    ## change % reads to rarefied % !!!!!!!  !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
  group_by(sample_id, primer) %>%
  mutate(rare_reads_sum=sum(rare_reads)) %>%
  mutate(percent_reads = rare_reads/rare_reads_sum)
  # !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

## ── Remove non-marine / contaminant taxa ─────────────────────────────────────
## Applied here so all downstream objects (euk_phylum, euk_order, and the
## per-primer supplementary figures) are clean.
## Join key mismatch: data lineages start with "Eukaryota;" (Superkingdom field
## from tl), but trait_dat lineages start at Kingdom ("Animalia;..."). Strip the
## leading superkingdom field into a temporary column for the join only.
dat_all_filt <- dat_all_filt %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(.lj = sub("^[^;]+;", "", lineage)) %>%
  left_join(dplyr::select(trait_dat, lineage, not_marine_contam),
            by = c(".lj" = "lineage")) %>%
  dplyr::filter(is.na(not_marine_contam) | not_marine_contam != 1) %>%
  dplyr::select(-not_marine_contam, -.lj)


# get list of samples that have both primers - some samples removed by low reads, then use below
samples_both_prim <- dat_all_filt %>% 
      distinct(primer,sample_id) %>% 
      group_by(sample_id) %>% 
      summarise(num_primers_sample=n()) %>% 
      filter(num_primers_sample >1)




# tidy above to make one df of all taxa present for both primers
# cluster_num was stripped above so same taxon from both primers now shares
# the same lineage string and collapses correctly in the group_by.
# percent_reads = MEAN across primers (average signal across primers for each taxon).
dat_all_filt_combine_prim <- dat_all_filt %>%   # names(dat_all_filt)
  group_by(lineage, sample_id, type, date, year, season, area, habitat, lat, lon, depth) %>%
  summarize(
    percent_reads    = mean(percent_reads),
    count_of_primers = n_distinct(primer),
    .groups          = "drop"
  ) %>%
  arrange(sample_id) %>%
  tidyr::separate(lineage, into=tl, sep=";" , remove=FALSE) %>%
  # remove samples that don't have both primers
  inner_join(select(samples_both_prim, sample_id))

## ---- assign global N→S sample numbers (1 = northernmost) -------------------
## Numbers are consistent across all habitats so that y-axis positions in
## faceted bar plots share the same scale, creating natural gaps where a
## habitat has no sample at a given latitude rank.
ns_sample_nums <- dat_all_filt_combine_prim %>%
  distinct(sample_id, lat) %>%
  arrange(desc(lat)) %>%
  mutate(sample_num_ns = row_number()) %>%
  select(sample_id, sample_num_ns)

dat_all_filt_combine_prim <- dat_all_filt_combine_prim %>%
  left_join(ns_sample_nums, by = "sample_id")


```

## Primer combine audit
Checks that the primer combination in `dat_all_filt_combine_prim` is working
correctly. Key concern: residual cluster numbers in `lineage` (from the decon
pipeline) would make the same taxon look different across primers and prevent
collapsing. Run this after every change to the `tiding` chunk.

```{r primer_combine_audit}
## ── 1. Residual cluster-number check ─────────────────────────────────────────
## Any lineage ending in ;digits means the strip regex didn't fire.
## This MUST be zero — if not, fix the lineage strip in tiding first.
n_cluster_suffix <- dat_all_filt %>%
  distinct(lineage) %>%
  filter(grepl(";-?\\d+$", lineage)) %>%
  nrow()
cat(sprintf("Lineages with residual cluster suffix (must be 0): %d\n\n",
            n_cluster_suffix))

## ── 2. Unique taxa per primer (before combining) ──────────────────────────────
taxa_per_primer <- dat_all_filt %>%
  filter(type == "sample") %>%
  group_by(primer) %>%
  summarise(n_taxa = n_distinct(lineage), n_samples = n_distinct(sample_id),
            .groups = "drop")
cat("Taxa and samples per primer (before combining):\n")
print(taxa_per_primer)
cat("\n")

## ── 3. Primer overlap — shared vs unique taxa ─────────────────────────────────
taxa_18sv9  <- dat_all_filt %>% filter(primer == "18S_V9", type == "sample") %>%
  distinct(lineage) %>% pull(lineage)
taxa_18sv7  <- dat_all_filt %>% filter(primer == "18S_V7", type == "sample") %>%
  distinct(lineage) %>% pull(lineage)

n_shared    <- length(intersect(taxa_18sv9, taxa_18sv7))
n_only_v9   <- length(setdiff(taxa_18sv9,  taxa_18sv7))
n_only_v7   <- length(setdiff(taxa_18sv7,  taxa_18sv9))
n_combined  <- length(union(taxa_18sv9,    taxa_18sv7))

cat(sprintf(
  "Taxon overlap across primers:\n  Shared (both primers):   %d\n  18S_V9 only:             %d\n  18S_V7 only:             %d\n  Union (all unique taxa): %d\n\n",
  n_shared, n_only_v9, n_only_v7, n_combined
))

## ── 4. After combining: count_of_primers distribution ────────────────────────
## count_of_primers == 2 → taxon detected by both; == 1 → one primer only.
## After inner_join(samples_both_prim), all samples have both primers, but
## individual taxa within a sample may still come from one primer only.
cat("count_of_primers distribution in dat_all_filt_combine_prim:\n")
print(table(dat_all_filt_combine_prim$count_of_primers))
cat("\n")

## ── 5. Total unique taxa after combining ─────────────────────────────────────
n_taxa_combined <- n_distinct(dat_all_filt_combine_prim$lineage)
n_samples_final <- n_distinct(dat_all_filt_combine_prim$sample_id)
cat(sprintf("Final combined dataset: %d unique taxa across %d samples\n\n",
            n_taxa_combined, n_samples_final))

## ── 6. Samples lost at each filtering stage ──────────────────────────────────
n_before_readfilt <- dat_all_filt %>%
  filter(type == "sample", !grepl("rep", sample_id)) %>%
  distinct(primer, sample_id) %>%
  group_by(sample_id) %>%
  summarise(n_prim = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  nrow()

n_both_primers <- nrow(samples_both_prim)
n_final        <- n_distinct(dat_all_filt_combine_prim$sample_id)

cat(sprintf(
  "Sample retention:\n  After read filter:           %d\n  With both primers present:   %d\n  Final (after combine):       %d\n  Dropped (one primer only):   %d\n\n",
  n_before_readfilt, n_both_primers, n_final,
  n_before_readfilt - n_both_primers
))

## ── 7. Taxa in combined set vs union of per-primer sets ──────────────────────
## If lineage strip worked, combined taxa should be ≤ union (some taxa lost
## because they only occur in samples that failed the both-primers filter).
## Combined taxa should NEVER exceed the union — flag if so.
if (n_taxa_combined > n_combined) {
  warning(sprintf(
    "PROBLEM: combined has MORE unique taxa (%d) than the union of per-primer sets (%d).\nThis suggests lineage strings still differ between primers — check cluster suffix strip.",
    n_taxa_combined, n_combined
  ))
} else {
  cat(sprintf(
    "Lineage consistency check OK: combined taxa (%d) ≤ per-primer union (%d)\n",
    n_taxa_combined, n_combined
  ))
}

## ── 8. Top taxa detected by only one primer ───────────────────────────────────
## High-abundance single-primer taxa may warrant investigation.
cat("\nTop 10 taxa unique to 18S_V9 (by mean percent_reads):\n")
dat_all_filt %>%
  filter(primer == "18S_V9", type == "sample",
         lineage %in% setdiff(taxa_18sv9, taxa_18sv7)) %>%
  group_by(lineage) %>%
  summarise(mean_pct = mean(percent_reads, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  slice_max(mean_pct, n = 10) %>%
  tidyr::separate(lineage, into = tl, sep = ";", remove = FALSE) %>%
  select(Order, Family, Genus, Species, mean_pct) %>%
  print()

cat("\nTop 10 taxa unique to 18S_V7 (by mean percent_reads):\n")
dat_all_filt %>%
  filter(primer == "18S_V7", type == "sample",
         lineage %in% setdiff(taxa_18sv7, taxa_18sv9)) %>%
  group_by(lineage) %>%
  summarise(mean_pct = mean(percent_reads, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  slice_max(mean_pct, n = 10) %>%
  tidyr::separate(lineage, into = tl, sep = ";", remove = FALSE) %>%
  select(Order, Family, Genus, Species, mean_pct) %>%
  print()
```

## compare mean vs max primer combine
Decision made: use MEAN. Kept for reference only — not run.

```{r compare_primers, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}


# 1. Extract ORDER from taxonomy string
dat_orders <- dat_all_filt_combine_prim %>%

  filter(!is.na(Order))

# 2. Summarize across all samples
# NOTE: percent_read_max no longer exists — pipeline was fixed to use MEAN.
# Both columns now show the same values; chunk kept for reference only.
dat_orders_sum <- dat_orders %>%
  group_by(Order) %>%
  summarise(
    mean_abund = mean(percent_reads, na.rm = TRUE),
    max_abund  = mean(percent_reads, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 3. Get top 20 orders (based on mean version)
top_orders <- dat_orders_sum %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_abund)) %>%
  slice(1:20) %>%
  pull(Order)

# 4. Keep only top 20 and reshape for plotting
dat_plot <- dat_orders_sum %>%
  filter(Order %in% top_orders) %>%
  pivot_longer(cols = c(mean_abund, max_abund),
               names_to = "method",
               values_to = "abundance") %>%
  mutate(method = dplyr::recode(method,
                         mean_abund = "Mean",
                         max_abund  = "Max"))

# 5. Plot
ggplot(dat_plot, aes(x = abundance,
                     y = fct_reorder(Order, abundance),
                     fill = method)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  labs(x = "Relative read proportion",
       y = "Order",
       fill = "Combination method",
       title = "Top 20 Orders: Mean vs Max Across Primers") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(text = element_text(size = 12))
```

## Sample drop audit
Cross-checks every sample in the metadata against each filtering stage so you can see exactly where samples were lost and why.
Produces `drop_audit_df` (one row per sample) and `drop_audit_summary` (counts by habitat × drop stage).

```{r sample_drop_audit}

# ── Ground truth: all intended samples from metadata ─────────────────────────
# Excludes rep entries (kept separately in the metadata sheet but not analysed).
sam_meta <- readxl::read_excel(sam_file_path, sheet = "sample_data") %>%
  dplyr::rename(sample_id = sample_ID) %>%
  filter(!grepl("rep", sample_id, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
  select(sample_id, HABITAT, AREA, YEAR, SEASON) %>%
  dplyr::rename(habitat_meta = HABITAT, area_meta = AREA,
                year_meta = YEAR, season_meta = SEASON)

# ── Stage flags ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Stage 1: sample_id appears anywhere in the raw sequence CSV
in_dat <- dat %>%
  filter(type == "sample", !grepl("rep", sample_id, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
  distinct(sample_id) %>%
  mutate(in_dat = TRUE)

# Stage 2: at least one row survives minboot==70 + 18S primer filter
in_18s_minboot <- dat %>%
  filter(type == "sample",
         !grepl("rep", sample_id, ignore.case = TRUE),
         minboot == 70,
         grepl("18S|18smini|euka", primer, ignore.case = TRUE)) %>%
  distinct(sample_id) %>%
  mutate(in_18s_minboot = TRUE)

# Stage 3: per-sample x primer read sums — determines which primer(s) survive
#          the low-reads threshold (50% of Q1 across samples)
reads_check <- dat_all %>%
  filter(type == "sample",
         !grepl("rep", sample_id, ignore.case = TRUE),
         grepl("18S", primer)) %>%
  distinct(sample_id, primer, primer_taxassign_id, sample_sum_after_filt) %>%
  left_join(min_reads_min, by = "primer_taxassign_id") %>%
  mutate(passes_reads = sample_sum_after_filt > fiftypercent_lower)

# Summarise: for each sample, how many primers pass?
reads_summary <- reads_check %>%
  group_by(sample_id) %>%
  summarise(
    n_primers_sequenced = n(),
    n_primers_pass      = sum(passes_reads),
    primers_fail        = paste(primer[!passes_reads],
                                paste0("(", round(sample_sum_after_filt[!passes_reads]), " reads)"),
                                collapse = "; "),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(primers_fail = if_else(primers_fail == "", "—", primers_fail))

# Stage 4: sample has both primers after read filter (samples_both_prim)
in_both_prim <- samples_both_prim %>%
  mutate(in_both_prim = TRUE)

# ── Build audit table ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
drop_audit_df <- sam_meta %>%
  left_join(in_dat,          by = "sample_id") %>%
  left_join(in_18s_minboot,  by = "sample_id") %>%
  left_join(reads_summary,   by = "sample_id") %>%
  left_join(in_both_prim,    by = "sample_id") %>%
  mutate(
    in_final   = sample_id %in% dat_all_filt_combine_prim$sample_id,
    drop_stage = case_when(
      in_final                                                          ~ "retained",
      is.na(in_dat)                                                     ~ "not_in_sequence_data",
      is.na(in_18s_minboot)                                             ~ "no_18S_reads_at_minboot70",
      !is.na(n_primers_pass) & n_primers_pass == 0                      ~ "low_reads_both_primers",
      !is.na(n_primers_pass) & n_primers_pass < n_primers_sequenced     ~ "low_reads_one_primer",
      is.na(in_both_prim)                                               ~ "only_one_primer_sequenced",
      TRUE                                                              ~ "unknown"
    )
  )

# ── Summary table: counts by habitat x drop stage ────────────────────────────
drop_audit_summary <- drop_audit_df %>%
  group_by(habitat_meta, drop_stage) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = drop_stage, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) %>%
  select(habitat_meta,
         any_of(c("retained",
                  "not_in_sequence_data",
                  "no_18S_reads_at_minboot70",
                  "low_reads_both_primers",
                  "low_reads_one_primer",
                  "only_one_primer_sequenced",
                  "unknown"))) %>%
  mutate(total_in_metadata = rowSums(across(where(is.numeric))),
         pct_retained = round(retained / total_in_metadata * 100, 1))

print(drop_audit_summary)

# ── Per-sample detail for dropped samples ─────────────────────────────────────
drop_audit_dropped <- drop_audit_df %>%
  filter(drop_stage != "retained") %>%
  select(sample_id, habitat_meta, area_meta, year_meta,
         drop_stage, primers_fail) %>%
  arrange(habitat_meta, drop_stage, sample_id)

print(drop_audit_dropped)

```

## Eukaryote by phylum

```{r euk_phylum}
#   use dat_all_filt
#  pool to phylum  !!!!!   get only needed data - keys, phylums, reads
euk_phylum<- dat_all_filt %>%  #  names(dat_all_filt)
  # break out lineage
  tidyr::separate(lineage, into=tl, sep=";" , remove=FALSE)   %>% 
  #
  select(habitat, primer, primer_taxassign_id, sample_id_u, year,season,area,lat,lon,depth ,Phylum, reads, rare_reads, percent_reads ) %>% 
  #  pool reads at phylum
  group_by(habitat, primer, primer_taxassign_id, sample_id_u, year,season,area,lat,lon,depth ,Phylum,) %>% 
  summarise(reads_new=sum(reads), rare_reads_new=sum(rare_reads), percent_reads= sum(percent_reads), rich_reads= length(reads[reads>0]), rich_rare_reads= length(reads[rare_reads>0]), n=n() ) %>% ## cannot use reads again or will mess up calcs - need new_
  filter(Phylum !="NA") %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  rename(reads=reads_new, rare_reads = rare_reads_new) %>% 
  droplevels()

## rank phylum by %
euk_phylum_rank <- euk_phylum %>%
  group_by(Phylum) %>%
  summarise(max_reads = max(percent_reads),mean = mean(percent_reads), median=median(percent_reads), n = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(median)) %>%
  filter( n > 10) %>% # filter phyla to only include those with this many samples
  pull(Phylum)

##  determine how many phyla to include
n<-15
euk_phylum_rank<-euk_phylum_rank[1:n]

## order by previous
euk_phylum_top <- euk_phylum %>%
  filter(Phylum %in% euk_phylum_rank) %>%
  mutate(Phylum = factor(Phylum, levels = euk_phylum_rank)) %>%
  arrange(Phylum) %>% 
   ungroup() 
  #mutate(ybp=as.integer(ybp))  # made some slices taht same !



#########################################################
#########################################################
#     pool primers   !!!!!
#########################################################

euk_phylum_combine_prim <- euk_phylum %>%   # names(euk_phylum)  names(euk_phylum_combine_prim)
  #  select
  separate(sample_id_u, c("primer", "sample_id", "minboot"), sep = ";") %>%
  select(-primer, -minboot) %>%
  group_by(sample_id,habitat, year,  season,area, lat,lon,depth, Phylum) %>% 
  summarize(percent_reads=mean(percent_reads), count_of_primers=n()  ) %>% 
  arrange(sample_id)

## rank phylum by %
euk_phylum_rank_combine_prim <- euk_phylum_combine_prim %>%
  group_by(Phylum) %>%
  summarise(max_reads = max(percent_reads),mean = mean(percent_reads), median=median(percent_reads), n = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(median)) %>%
  filter( n > 10) %>% # filter phyla to only include those with this many samples
  pull(Phylum)

##  determine how many phyla to include
n<-15
euk_phylum_rank_combine_prim<-euk_phylum_rank_combine_prim[1:n]

## order by previous — use the combine-primer rank (not the per-primer rank)
euk_phylum_top_combine_prim <- euk_phylum_combine_prim %>%
  filter(Phylum %in% euk_phylum_rank_combine_prim) %>%
  mutate(Phylum = factor(Phylum, levels = euk_phylum_rank_combine_prim)) %>%
  arrange(Phylum) %>%
   ungroup()
```

## Metazoan by order

```{r animal}
#   use dat_all_filt
# limit to metaz and recalc percent, get richness and diversity
#  pool to order  !!!!!   get only needed data - keys, phylums, reads



## make pattern for filtering
metaz_pat<-c("Annelida","Arthropoda","Chordata","Cnidaria","Ctenophora","Echinodermata","Gastrotricha","Mollusca","Nematoda","Orthonectida","Platyhelminthes","Porifera","Rotifera","Sipuncula","Tardigrada","Urochordata","Chaetognatha","Craniata","Nemertea","Bryozoa","Hemichordata","Brachiopoda","Entoprocta","Cephalochordata","Entoprocta","Gnathostomulida", "Xenacoelomorpha") 
metaz_pat<-paste(metaz_pat, collapse = "|")



# limit to metazoan phyla then get reads per sample and % per taxa
metaz_order <- euk_order %>%   # names(euk_genus)  unique(dat3$habitat)
  filter(grepl(metaz_pat, Phylum))  %>%  # limit to metaz phyla
    filter(Order !="NA") %>% 
  select(-rare_reads,-percent_reads, -rich_reads, -rich_rare_reads, -n) %>% 
  #unite("lineage", Phylum:Order, sep = ";", remove = FALSE) %>% 
  #group_by(primer, core, ybp) %>% 
    #  pool reads at genus
  group_by( primer, primer_taxassign_id,sample_id_u,lat,lon,depth) %>% 
  mutate(sum_metaz_reads = sum(reads)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(percent_reads = (reads / sum_metaz_reads)  * 100) %>% 
  #  !!!!!!  remove if sample has less than 100 metazoan reads  !!!
  filter(sum_metaz_reads >= 100) %>% 
  #rename(reads=reads_new, rare_reads = rare_reads_new) %>% 
  droplevels()

## rank g by %
metaz_order_rank <- metaz_order %>%
  group_by(Phylum,Class, Order) %>%
  summarise(max_reads = max(percent_reads),mean = mean(percent_reads), median=median(percent_reads), n = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(median)) %>%
  filter( n > 3) %>% # filter g to only include those with this many samples
  pull(Order)

##  determine how many to include
n<-15
metaz_order_rank<-metaz_order_rank[1:n]

## order an dlimit by previous
metaz_order_top <- metaz_order %>%
  filter(Order %in% metaz_order_rank) %>%
  mutate(Order = factor(Order, levels = metaz_order_rank)) %>%
  arrange(Order) %>% 
   ungroup() 
  #mutate(ybp=as.integer(ybp))  # made some slices taht same !

#########################################################
#########################################################
#   for  pooled primers   !!!!!
#########################################################
# use combined primers - removed samples that had only 1 primer

# sum by selected lineage
metaz_order_combine_prim <- euk_order_combine_prim %>%   # names(metaz_phylum)  names(metaz_phylum_combine_prim)
  # limit to metazoan phylums
    filter(grepl(metaz_pat, Phylum))  %>%  # limit to metaz phyla
    filter(Order !="NA") %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  #  select
  group_by(sample_id, lat,lon,depth) %>% 
  
    mutate(sum_metaz_reads = sum(percent_reads)) %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(percent_reads2 = (percent_reads/ sum_metaz_reads)  * 100 , count_of_primers=n() ) %>% 
  #  !!!!!!  remove if sample has less than 100 metazoan reads  !!!
  filter(sum_metaz_reads >= 1) %>% 
  select(-percent_reads, -count_of_primers)  %>% 
  rename(percent_reads = percent_reads2) %>% 
  droplevels() %>% 
  arrange(sample_id)

## rank phylum by %
metaz_order_rank_combine_prim <- metaz_order_combine_prim %>%
  group_by(Phylum, Class, Order) %>%
  summarise(max_reads = max(percent_reads),mean = mean(percent_reads), median=median(percent_reads), n = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(median)) %>%
  filter( n > 3) %>% # filter order to only include those with this many samples
  pull(Order)

##  determine how many phyla to include
n<-15
metaz_order_rank_combine_prim<-metaz_order_rank_combine_prim[1:n]

## order by previous — use the combine-primer rank      unique(metaz_order_top_combine_prim$Order)

  filter(Order %in% metaz_order_rank_combine_prim) %>%
  mutate(Order = factor(Order, levels = metaz_order_rank_combine_prim)) %>%
  arrange(Order) %>%
```

## Fig 1 — Sampling map
Composite figure: full Red Sea overview (left) + 4 zoomed area panels (right).
Original 7 boxes (a–g) merged into 4 geographic groups:
  a  = old a + b  (northern Red Sea, Duba/Qasabah area)
  b  = old c      (Al Wajh / Farasan Bank)
  c  = old d + e  (Yanbu / Thuwal)
  d  = old f + g  (Al Lith / Farasan south)
Box extents expanded relative to originals to include previously clipped samples:
  a: xmax extended to 36.15 (captures DC 2016/2017 M1 mangroves at lon 36.011)
  b: ymin lowered to 25.05 (captures CCF_S 2017 AW SG at lat 25.157)
  d: xmax extended to 41.70 (captures DC 2017 S6/S7/S8/S9/M4 up to lon 41.57)
     ymax raised to 20.25 (captures DC 2016 S6 at lat 20.160)
Panels a–b stacked in middle column; c–d stacked in right column.
All zoom panels have solid black borders.
```{r sampling_map}
## patchwork is loaded in the libraries chunk

## ensure plots subfolder exists
dir.create(paste0(dir, plot_file), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

## ---- sample locations -------------------------------------------------------
## Fixed seed so jitter offsets are identical across overview and zoom panels,
## keeping points and their text labels spatially consistent.
set.seed(42)
loc_data <- dat_all_filt_combine_prim %>%
  distinct(sample_id, lat, lon, habitat, sample_num_ns) %>%
  filter(!is.na(lat), !is.na(lon), !is.na(habitat)) %>%
  mutate(
    habitat = factor(habitat, levels = c("Coral", "Mangrove", "Seagrass")),
    ## small jitter (~0-4 km) separates co-located samples without misrepresenting geography
    lon_j   = jitter(lon, amount = 0.04),
    lat_j   = jitter(lat, amount = 0.04)
  )

## ---- colour scheme ----------------------------------------------------------
hab_cols <- c(
  "Coral"    = "#D73027",
  "Mangrove" = "#1A9A72",
  "Seagrass" = "#F5A623"
)

## ---- zoom-region bounding boxes (lon/lat) -----------------------------------
## 4 groups combining the original 7 boxes.
## Extents set to fully enclose all retained samples; make_zoom_panel adds
## a buf=0.10 margin beyond each edge when drawing the panel and filtering points.
## Panel labels: overview = a; zoom panels = b–e.
zoom_boxes <- list(
  # old a + b: northern Red Sea (Qasabah, Duba)
  # xmax extended to 36.15 to include M1 mangroves at lon 36.011
  b = c(xmin = 34.75, xmax = 36.15, ymin = 26.75, ymax = 28.15),

  # old c: Al Wajh / Farasan Bank cluster
  # ymin lowered to 25.05 to include CCF_S 2017 AW SG at lat 25.157
  c = c(xmin = 36.35, xmax = 37.25, ymin = 25.05, ymax = 26.10),

  # old d + e: Yanbu / Thuwal
  d = c(xmin = 37.75, xmax = 39.15, ymin = 21.90, ymax = 24.05),

  # old f + g: Al Lith / southern Farasan Banks
  # xmax extended to 41.70 to include DC 2017 S6/S7/S8/S9/M4 (up to lon 41.57)
  # ymax raised to 20.25 to include DC 2016 S6 at lat 20.160
  e = c(xmin = 39.75, xmax = 41.70, ymin = 17.75, ymax = 20.25)
)

## ---- sf polygons for overview boxes ----------------------------------------
box_polys <- purrr::imap(zoom_boxes, function(b, nm) {
  sf::st_sf(
    label    = nm,
    geometry = sf::st_sfc(sf::st_polygon(list(matrix(
      c(b["xmin"], b["ymin"], b["xmax"], b["ymin"],
        b["xmax"], b["ymax"], b["xmin"], b["ymax"],
        b["xmin"], b["ymin"]),
      ncol = 2, byrow = TRUE))), crs = 4326)
  )
}) %>% do.call(rbind, .)

label_df <- data.frame(
  label = names(zoom_boxes),
  x     = sapply(zoom_boxes, `[[`, "xmax"),
  y     = sapply(zoom_boxes, `[[`, "ymax")
)

## ---- overview map -----------------------------------------------------------
p_overview <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = me, fill = "grey90", colour = "grey60", linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_sf(data = box_polys, fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.45) +
  geom_text(data = label_df, aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
            hjust = 0, vjust = -0.25, size = 4.5) +
  geom_point(data = loc_data,
             aes(x = lon_j, y = lat_j, colour = habitat), size = 1.6, alpha = 0.65) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = hab_cols, name = "Habitat") +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(32, 44), ylim = c(10, 30), expand = FALSE) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Latitude") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 9) +
  theme(
    legend.position      = c(0.19, 0.28),
    legend.background    = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "grey80", linewidth = 0.4),
    legend.key           = element_blank(),
    legend.title         = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold"),
    legend.text          = element_text(size = 11),
    panel.border         = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.6),
    panel.background     = element_rect(fill = "#D6EAF8"),
    axis.text            = element_text(size = 11),
    axis.title.y         = element_text(size = 11),
    ## right margin = 0 pulls the zoom grid flush
    plot.margin          = margin(5, 0, 5, 5)
  )

## ---- inset locator map (top-right corner of overview) -----------------------
## Shows wider Arabian Peninsula region; black rectangle marks the overview extent.
## Uses world (medium scale) — sufficient detail at this zoom level.
p_inset <- ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = world, fill = "grey85", colour = "grey50", linewidth = 0.15) +
  annotate("rect",
           xmin = 34.75, xmax = 41.70, ymin = 17.75, ymax = 28.15,
           fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.9) +
  coord_sf(xlim = c(20, 65), ylim = c(5, 45), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void() +
  theme(
    panel.border     = element_rect(fill = NA, colour = "black", linewidth = 0.7),
    panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#D6EAF8"),
    plot.background  = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = NA)
  )

## scale bar + panel label "a" while p_overview is still a plain ggplot.
## The "a" label MUST be added before inset_element: patchwork's + operator
## after inset_element attaches layers to the inset plot, not the base map.
p_overview <- p_overview +
  ggspatial::annotation_scale(
    location      = "br",
    width_hint    = 0.20,
    unit_category = "metric",
    style         = "bar",
    text_cex      = 0.85,
    pad_x         = unit(0.25, "cm"),
    pad_y         = unit(0.25, "cm")
  ) +
  annotate("text", x = 32.15, y = 29.75, label = "a",
           hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 4.5)

## embed inset — p_overview becomes a patchwork object after this line
p_overview <- p_overview +
  inset_element(p_inset,
                left = 0.60, bottom = 0.72, right = 1.00, top = 1.00,
                align_to = "panel")

## ---- helper: single zoom panel (with km scale bar) -------------------------
make_zoom_panel <- function(label, box, loc, basemap, cols, buf = 0.10) {
  sub_loc <- loc %>%
    filter(lon >= box["xmin"] - buf, lon <= box["xmax"] + buf,
           lat >= box["ymin"] - buf, lat <= box["ymax"] + buf)
  # ~3 evenly-spaced tick labels per axis; pretty() picks clean round values
  x_breaks <- pretty(c(box["xmin"] - buf, box["xmax"] + buf), n = 3)
  y_breaks <- pretty(c(box["ymin"] - buf, box["ymax"] + buf), n = 3)
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = basemap, fill = "grey90", colour = "grey40", linewidth = 0.30) +
    geom_point(data = sub_loc,
               aes(x = lon_j, y = lat_j, colour = habitat), size = 2.6, alpha = 0.70) +
    ggrepel::geom_text_repel(data = sub_loc,
               aes(x = lon_j, y = lat_j, label = sample_num_ns),
               size = 2.5, colour = "black", fontface = "bold",
               box.padding = 0.25, point.padding = 0.15,
               min.segment.length = 0.3, max.overlaps = Inf,
               segment.colour = "grey50", segment.size = 0.3) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = cols, guide = "none") +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = x_breaks) +
    scale_y_continuous(breaks = y_breaks) +
    ggspatial::annotation_scale(
      location      = "br",
      width_hint    = 0.30,
      unit_category = "metric",
      style         = "bar",
      text_cex      = 0.80,
      pad_x         = unit(0.15, "cm"),
      pad_y         = unit(0.15, "cm")
    ) +
    coord_sf(xlim = c(box["xmin"] - buf, box["xmax"] + buf),
             ylim = c(box["ymin"] - buf, box["ymax"] + buf), expand = FALSE) +
    annotate("text", x = box["xmin"] - buf + 0.07, y = box["ymax"] + buf - 0.07,
             label = label, hjust = 0, vjust = 1, size = 4.5) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(
      panel.border     = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 1.3),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#D6EAF8"),
      axis.text        = element_text(size = 10),
      axis.ticks       = element_line(linewidth = 0.25),
      plot.margin      = margin(3, 3, 3, 3)
    )
}

## ---- build all 4 panels -----------------------------------------------------
zoom_panels <- mapply(make_zoom_panel,
  label    = names(zoom_boxes),
  box      = zoom_boxes,
  MoreArgs = list(loc = loc_data, basemap = me, cols = hab_cols),
  SIMPLIFY = FALSE)

## ---- zoom panel margins and axis labels -------------------------------------
## Left margin = 0 on the left-column panels (b, d) pulls them flush against
## the overview. Add Longitude title to bottom-row panels (d, e) only.
zoom_panels[["b"]] <- zoom_panels[["b"]] + theme(plot.margin = margin(3, 3, 3, 0))
zoom_panels[["d"]] <- zoom_panels[["d"]] + theme(plot.margin = margin(3, 3, 3, 0))

## ---- compose ----------------------------------------------------------------
zoom_grid <- (zoom_panels[["b"]] | zoom_panels[["c"]]) /
             (zoom_panels[["d"]] | zoom_panels[["e"]])

inner <- (p_overview | zoom_grid) + plot_layout(widths = c(2.2, 2.0))

## ---- single x-axis label ----------------------------------------------------
## wrap_elements strip works for x because the gap is just the bottom plot
## margin — no tick-label area in the way (unlike the y-axis side).
## inner is treated as one unit by /, so x_lab spans the full figure width.
x_lab <- wrap_elements(
  panel = grid::textGrob("Longitude", gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 11))
) + theme(plot.margin = margin(0, 0, 0, 0))

sampling_map <- (inner / x_lab) + plot_layout(heights = c(1, 0.04))

sampling_map

ggsave(paste0(dir, plot_file, "/RS_surface_sampling_map.tiff"),
       sampling_map, width = 34, height = 22, units = "cm", dpi = 300)
```




## Figs 2 & 3 — Bar plot helpers

```{r barplot_helpers}
## ---- Helper: order sample_id factor N→S (north/high-lat at top) ------------
## Within each call, samples are ranked by mean lat (desc = north is first /
## plotted at the top of the y-axis in a horizontal bar chart).
ns_order <- function(df, id_col = "sample_id") {
  df %>%
    group_by(!!sym(id_col)) %>%
    mutate(.lat_mean = mean(lat, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(!!sym(id_col) := forcats::fct_reorder(
      !!sym(id_col), .lat_mean, .desc = FALSE))
  # .desc=FALSE → lowest lat (south) gets factor level 1, plotted at bottom;
  # ggplot y-axis is drawn bottom-to-top, so north ends up at top.
}

## ---- Shared ggplot theme for bar figures ------------------------------------
theme_bar <- function(base = 10) {
  theme_bw(base_size = base) +
    theme(
      panel.border     = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.8),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey90", colour = "black"),
      strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold"),
      axis.text.y      = element_text(size = 6),
      legend.position  = "right",
      legend.key.size  = unit(0.35, "cm"),
      legend.text      = element_text(size = 8),
      plot.caption     = element_text(size = 7, colour = "grey50")
    )
}

## ---- Colour palettes (15 distinct colours each) -----------------------------
## Phylum palette — ordered to match euk_phylum_rank_combine_prim
phylum_pal <- c(
"#7f265b","#5dbb68","#58388b","#9eb13f","#677fd8","#ca913b","#bc80d5","#45bc8d","#c9417e","#36dee6","#ba4758","#758a3c","#c25bac","#b75636","#da75a0"
)


phylum_fill <- setNames(
  phylum_pal[seq_along(euk_phylum_rank_combine_prim)],
  euk_phylum_rank_combine_prim
)

## Order palette — ordered to match euk_order_rank_combine_prim
order_pal <- c(
"#7f265b","#5dbb68","#58388b","#9eb13f","#677fd8","#ca913b","#bc80d5","#45bc8d","#c9417e","#36dee6","#ba4758","#758a3c","#c25bac","#b75636","#da75a0"
)
order_fill <- setNames(
  order_pal[seq_along(euk_order_rank_combine_prim)],
  euk_order_rank_combine_prim
)

## ---- Shared zone-divider positions (reused in fig2 and fig3) ---------------
## Midpoints of the lat gaps between the 4 map zoom boxes (a/b/c/d, N→S):
##   a (ymin 26.75) / b (ymax 26.10) → cut 26.425
##   b (ymin 25.05) / c (ymax 24.05) → cut 24.550
##   c (ymin 21.90) / d (ymax 20.25) → cut 21.075
zone_lat_cuts <- c((26.75 + 26.10) / 2,
                   (25.05 + 24.05) / 2,
                   (21.90 + 20.25) / 2)

.ns_lat_lkp <- dat_all_filt_combine_prim %>%
  distinct(sample_id, lat) %>%
  inner_join(ns_sample_nums, by = "sample_id") %>%
  arrange(sample_num_ns)

zone_lines <- sapply(zone_lat_cuts, function(cut_lat) {
  above <- .ns_lat_lkp %>% filter(lat >  cut_lat) %>%
              slice_max(sample_num_ns, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
              pull(sample_num_ns)
  below <- .ns_lat_lkp %>% filter(lat <= cut_lat) %>%
              slice_min(sample_num_ns, n = 1, with_ties = FALSE) %>%
              pull(sample_num_ns)
  if (!length(above) || !length(below)) return(NA_real_)
  (above + below) / 2
}) %>% na.omit()

## zone centre positions for letter labels (a–d), used in fig2 & fig3
n_max_ns <- max(ns_sample_nums$sample_num_ns)
zone_label_df <- tibble::tibble(
  y_pos = c(mean(c(1,            zone_lines[1])),
            mean(zone_lines[c(1, 2)]),
            mean(zone_lines[c(2, 3)]),
            mean(c(zone_lines[3], n_max_ns))),
  label = c("a", "b", "c", "d")
)
```


## Fig 2 — Phylum bar plots

```{r fig2_phylum}
## ensure the plots output folder exists regardless of chunk run order
dir.create(paste0(dir, plot_file), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

## ---- prepare data -----------------------------------------------------------
## Join global N→S sample numbers so y-axis positions are consistent across
## habitat panels — gaps appear naturally where a habitat lacks samples at
## a given latitude rank (matching manuscript Fig. 2 layout).
plot_dat_phylum <- euk_phylum_top_combine_prim %>%
  filter(!is.na(habitat), !is.na(Phylum)) %>%
  left_join(ns_sample_nums, by = "sample_id") %>%
  filter(!is.na(sample_num_ns))           # drop any samples not in filtered set

## Pre-compute cumulative stacked x-positions per sample.
## geom_col/position_stack() does not work reliably with a continuous numeric
## y-axis (produces warnings and negative bars); geom_rect() with explicit
## xmin/xmax fully bypasses position_stack().
plot_dat_phylum_stk <- plot_dat_phylum %>%
  arrange(sample_num_ns, Phylum) %>%
  group_by(sample_num_ns, habitat) %>%
  mutate(
    xmax = cumsum(percent_reads),
    xmin = xmax - percent_reads
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

## zone_lines and zone_label_df are computed in the barplot_helpers chunk.

## ---- zone letters for right-side annotation (Seagrass panel only) ----------
## Placed at x = Inf so they sit just outside the right edge of each panel;
## coord_cartesian(clip = "off") + wider right margin make them visible.
## Filtering to "Seagrass" (rightmost facet) gives a single right-side axis.
zone_label_right <- zone_label_df %>%
  mutate(habitat = factor("Seagrass", levels = c("Coral", "Mangrove", "Seagrass")))

## ---- main figure (3-panel: habitat) matching manuscript Fig. 2 -------------
## y-axis: continuous N→S sample number (1 = northernmost).
## facet_grid(. ~ habitat, scales = "free"): each panel has its own x and y
##   range, so gaps appear between non-consecutive sample numbers.
## Three dashed lines divide the plot into the 4 geographic zones from Fig. 1.
fig2 <- ggplot(plot_dat_phylum_stk) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = zone_lines,
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax,
                ymin = sample_num_ns - 0.40, ymax = sample_num_ns + 0.40,
                fill = Phylum)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = phylum_fill, na.value = "grey85") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0),
                     labels = scales::percent) +
  ## Reversed so sample 1 (northernmost) sits at the top of each panel.
  ## Integer breaks only (ceiling/floor), 0 excluded; check.overlap drops
  ## labels that would collide at this font size.
  scale_y_reverse(
    breaks = function(lims) {
      b <- seq(ceiling(min(lims)), floor(max(lims)))
      b[b > 0]
    },
    expand = expansion(add = 0.5),
    guide  = guide_axis(check.overlap = TRUE)
  ) +
  geom_text(data = zone_label_right,
            aes(x = Inf, y = y_pos, label = label),
            inherit.aes = FALSE,
            hjust = -0.4, colour = "grey25", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5) +
  coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
  facet_grid(. ~ habitat, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Relative abundance (%)", y = "Sample (N \u2192 S)", fill = "Phylum") +
  theme_bar() +
  theme(axis.text.y  = element_text(size = 7),
        plot.margin  = margin(5, 30, 5, 5))

fig2

ggsave(paste0(dir, plot_file, "/Fig2_phylum_barplot.tiff"),
       fig2, width = 24, height = 23, units = "cm", dpi = 300)

## ---- supplementary: per primer (rows = habitat, columns = primer) -----------
## Primers paired horizontally (columns) so the two primers for each habitat
## sit side-by-side, making within-habitat primer comparisons easy.
##
## Y-axis trick: convert sample_num_ns to a zero-padded character factor so
## the axis is DISCRETE. This means:
##   (a) facet_grid with scales="free_y" drops unused levels per row — each
##       habitat row is only as tall as its own sample count, no blank gaps.
##   (b) geom_col / position_stack() work correctly (they require discrete y).
## Zero-padding ("01","02"..."10") keeps lexicographic sort == numeric sort.
plot_dat_phylum_primer <- euk_phylum_top %>%
  filter(!is.na(habitat), !is.na(Phylum)) %>%
  separate(sample_id_u, c("mes1", "sample_id", "mes2"), sep = ";") %>%
  select(-mes1, -mes2) %>%
  left_join(ns_sample_nums, by = "sample_id") %>%
  filter(!is.na(sample_num_ns)) %>%
  mutate(sample_num_chr = factor(
    sprintf("%02d", sample_num_ns),
    levels = sprintf("%02d", sort(unique(sample_num_ns)))
  ))

## Zone lines for discrete y-axis: compute per-habitat yintercept in discrete
## position units. With limits=rev, disc_pos 1 = bottommost bar (largest
## sample_num_ns = southernmost); positions increase upward toward north.
## geom_hline with a `habitat` column in the data frame makes ggplot draw the
## line only in the correct habitat row of the facet_grid.
zone_hline_s2 <- {
  dp_lkp <- plot_dat_phylum_primer %>%
    distinct(habitat, sample_num_ns) %>%
    arrange(habitat, desc(sample_num_ns)) %>%
    group_by(habitat) %>%
    mutate(disc_pos = row_number()) %>%
    ungroup()

  purrr::map_dfr(zone_lines, function(zl) {
    dp_lkp %>%
      group_by(habitat) %>%
      summarise(
        ## disc_pos of the last sample on the north side of the boundary (≤ zl)
        p_a = { s <- sample_num_ns[sample_num_ns <= zl]
                d <- disc_pos[sample_num_ns <= zl]
                if (length(s) == 0L) NA_real_ else d[which.max(s)] },
        ## disc_pos of the first sample on the south side of the boundary (> zl)
        p_b = { s <- sample_num_ns[sample_num_ns > zl]
                d <- disc_pos[sample_num_ns > zl]
                if (length(s) == 0L) NA_real_ else d[which.min(s)] },
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      mutate(yintercept = (p_a + p_b) / 2) %>%
      select(habitat, yintercept) %>%
      filter(!is.na(yintercept))
  })
}

fig_s2_primer <- ggplot(plot_dat_phylum_primer,
                        aes(x = percent_reads, y = sample_num_chr, fill = Phylum)) +
  geom_hline(data = zone_hline_s2,
             aes(yintercept = yintercept),
             inherit.aes = FALSE,
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", width = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = phylum_fill, na.value = "grey85") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), labels = scales::percent) +
  ## limits = rev puts "01" at top (north); drop = TRUE removes unused levels
  ## so each habitat row only spans its own samples — no wasted vertical space.
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev, drop = TRUE) +
  facet_grid(habitat ~ primer, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Relative abundance (%)", y = "Sample (N \u2192 S)", fill = "Phylum",
       caption = "Supplementary: phylum composition by primer pair") +
  theme_bar(base = 10) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
        strip.text  = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9))

fig_s2_primer

ggsave(paste0(dir, plot_file, "/FigS_phylum_barplot_by_primer.tiff"),
       fig_s2_primer, width = 28, height = 32, units = "cm", dpi = 300)
```

```{r fig3_order}
dir.create(paste0(dir, plot_file), showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

## ---- prepare data -----------------------------------------------------------

## right-side zone labels for fig3 (same logic as fig2)
zone_label_right_o <- zone_label_df %>%
  mutate(habitat = factor("Seagrass", levels = c("Coral", "Mangrove", "Seagrass")))

## ---- main figure (3-panel: habitat) ----------------------------------------
fig3 <- ggplot(plot_dat_order_stk) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = zone_lines,
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_rect(aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax,

  scale_fill_manual(values = order_fill, na.value = "grey85") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_y_reverse(
    breaks = function(lims) { b <- seq(ceiling(min(lims)), floor(max(lims))); b[b > 0] },
    expand = expansion(add = 0.5),
    guide  = guide_axis(check.overlap = TRUE)
  ) +
  facet_grid(. ~ habitat, scales = "free") +
  labs(x = "Relative abundance (%)", y = "Sample (N \u2192 S)", fill = "Order") +
  theme_bar() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
        plot.margin  = margin(5, 30, 5, 5))

fig3

ggsave(paste0(dir, plot_file, "/Fig3_order_barplot.tiff"),
       fig3, width = 24, height = 23, units = "cm", dpi = 300)



## ---- supplementary: per primer (rows = habitat, columns = primer) -----------
## Same discrete-y trick as fig_s2_primer: zero-padded character factor so
## each habitat row only occupies as many bars as it has samples.
plot_dat_order_primer <- euk_order_top %>%
  filter(!is.na(habitat), !is.na(Order)) %>%
  separate(sample_id_u, c("mes1", "sample_id", "mes2"), sep = ";") %>%
  select(-mes1, -mes2) %>%
  left_join(ns_sample_nums, by = "sample_id") %>%
  filter(!is.na(sample_num_ns)) %>%
  mutate(sample_num_chr = factor(
    sprintf("%02d", sample_num_ns),
    levels = sprintf("%02d", sort(unique(sample_num_ns)))
  ))

## Zone lines for fig_s3_primer discrete y-axis (same approach as fig_s2_primer)
zone_hline_s3 <- {
  dp_lkp <- plot_dat_order_primer %>%
    distinct(habitat, sample_num_ns) %>%
    arrange(habitat, desc(sample_num_ns)) %>%
    group_by(habitat) %>%
    mutate(disc_pos = row_number()) %>%
    ungroup()

  purrr::map_dfr(zone_lines, function(zl) {
    dp_lkp %>%
      group_by(habitat) %>%
      summarise(
        p_a = { s <- sample_num_ns[sample_num_ns <= zl]
                d <- disc_pos[sample_num_ns <= zl]
                if (length(s) == 0L) NA_real_ else d[which.max(s)] },
        p_b = { s <- sample_num_ns[sample_num_ns > zl]
                d <- disc_pos[sample_num_ns > zl]
                if (length(s) == 0L) NA_real_ else d[which.min(s)] },
        .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
      mutate(yintercept = (p_a + p_b) / 2) %>%
      select(habitat, yintercept) %>%
      filter(!is.na(yintercept))
  })
}

fig_s3_primer <- ggplot(plot_dat_order_primer,
                        aes(x = percent_reads, y = sample_num_chr, fill = Order)) +
  geom_hline(data = zone_hline_s3,
             aes(yintercept = yintercept),
             inherit.aes = FALSE,
             linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", width = 0.8) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = order_fill, na.value = "grey85") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0), labels = scales::percent) +
  scale_y_discrete(limits = rev, drop = TRUE) +
  facet_grid(habitat ~ primer, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(x = "Relative abundance (%)", y = "Sample (N \u2192 S)", fill = "Order",
       caption = "Supplementary: top 15 orders by primer pair") +
  theme_bar(base = 10) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
        strip.text  = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9))

fig_s3_primer

ggsave(paste0(dir, plot_file, "/FigS_order_barplot_by_primer.tiff"),
       fig_s3_primer, width = 28, height = 32, units = "cm", dpi = 300)
```

## Fig — Metazoan class bar plots

```{r fig_metaz_class}
## ---- rebuild metazoan data without minimum-reads filter --------------------
## Includes all samples with any metazoan reads; pools to Class level.
metaz_zone_base <- euk_order_combine_prim %>%
  filter(grepl(metaz_pat, Phylum), !is.na(habitat),
         !is.na(Class), Class != "NA", trimws(Class) != "") %>%
  group_by(sample_id, lat, lon, habitat, Phylum, Class) %>%
  summarise(percent_reads = sum(percent_reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(sample_id) %>%
  mutate(sum_metaz = sum(percent_reads)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(sum_metaz > 0) %>%
  mutate(percent_reads = percent_reads / sum_metaz * 100)

## ---- top 15 classes by median across samples --------------------------------
metaz_class_rank <- metaz_zone_base %>%
  group_by(Class) %>%
  summarise(median = median(percent_reads), n = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(median)) %>%
  filter(n > 3) %>%
  slice_head(n = 15) %>%
  pull(Class)

## Colour palette keyed to class rank
metaz_class_fill <- setNames(order_pal[seq_along(metaz_class_rank)], metaz_class_rank)

## ---- filter to top 15 and assign zones --------------------------------------
metaz_zone_base <- metaz_zone_base %>%
  filter(Class %in% metaz_class_rank) %>%
  mutate(
    Class    = factor(Class, levels = metaz_class_rank),
    zone_agg = case_when(
      lat > zone_lat_cuts[1] ~ "a",
      lat > zone_lat_cuts[2] ~ "b",
      lat > zone_lat_cuts[3] ~ "c",
      TRUE                   ~ "d"
    ),
    zone_agg = factor(zone_agg, levels = c("d", "c", "b", "a")),
    habitat  = factor(habitat, levels = c("Coral", "Mangrove", "Seagrass"))
  )

## ---- mean: each sample weighted equally ------------------------------------
metaz_zone_mean <- metaz_zone_base %>%
  group_by(zone_agg, habitat, Class) %>%
  summarise(percent_reads = mean(percent_reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
  mutate(method = "Mean (equal sample weight)")

## ---- pooled sum: pool reads across samples, renormalize to 100% ------------
metaz_zone_pool <- metaz_zone_base %>%
  group_by(zone_agg, habitat, Class) %>%
  summarise(reads_sum = sum(percent_reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
  group_by(zone_agg, habitat) %>%
  mutate(percent_reads = reads_sum / sum(reads_sum) * 100) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(method = "Pooled sum (renormalized)")

metaz_zone_both <- bind_rows(metaz_zone_mean, metaz_zone_pool) %>%
  mutate(method = factor(method,
           levels = c("Mean (equal sample weight)", "Pooled sum (renormalized)")))

## ---- figure (2-row × 3-column: method × habitat) ---------------------------
fig_metaz_zone <- ggplot(metaz_zone_both,
                         aes(x = percent_reads, y = zone_agg, fill = Class)) +
  geom_col(position = "stack", width = 0.65) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = metaz_class_fill, na.value = "grey85") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0, 0),
                     labels = scales::label_number(suffix = "%")) +
  facet_grid(method ~ habitat, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Relative abundance (% of Metazoa)",
       y = "Zone (N → S)",
       fill = "Class") +
  theme_bar() +
  theme(strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10))

fig_metaz_zone

ggsave(paste0(dir, plot_file, "/Fig_metaz_class_zone.tiff"),
       fig_metaz_zone, width = 28, height = 18, units = "cm", dpi = 300)
```

## Richness and diversity stats
tests can take 40 min, run caffeinate -dims in terminal to keep computer awake, then CTRL+c to stop
```{r stat}

#### stats  ######

## Richness and Shannon recalculated from combined-primer data, matching the
## method in Red_Sea_post_DADA2_filter_and_tidy.Rmd:
##   rich_rare     = number of taxa with percent_reads > 0 per sample
##   shan_div_rare = vegan::diversity() on wide-format percent_reads matrix
comb_wide <- dat_all_filt_combine_prim %>%
  select(sample_id, lineage, percent_reads) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = lineage, values_from = percent_reads, values_fill = 0)

rich_shan <- tibble::tibble(
  sample_id     = comb_wide$sample_id,
  rich_rare     = rowSums(comb_wide[, -1] > 0),
  shan_div_rare = vegan::diversity(comb_wide[, -1], index = "shannon")
)

sdat <- dat_all_filt_combine_prim %>%
  distinct(sample_id, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  select(sample_id, year, season, area, habitat, lat, lon, depth) %>%
  left_join(rich_shan, by = "sample_id") %>%
  left_join(
    env %>% dplyr::select(sample_ID, sst_mean, SST_range, pp_mean, pp_range,
                          salinity, nitrate, land_distance, PAR),
    by = c("sample_id" = "sample_ID")
  ) %>%
  mutate(Latitude = lat, Longitude = lon,
         sample_id = as.factor(sample_id), area = as.factor(area)) %>%
  # mutate(y = rich_rare) # rich_rare or shan_div_rare
  mutate(y = rich_rare)
  
# levels(sdat$sample_id)  levels(sdat$area)

###scale scale=TRUE divides by the standard deviation default does both center and scale
names(sdat)
sdat$sTemp<-scale(sdat$sst_mean)
sdat$sSST_range<-scale(sdat$SST_range)
sdat$sland_distance<-scale(sdat$land_distance)
sdat$slat<-scale(sdat$lat)
sdat$spp<-scale(sdat$pp_mean)
sdat$spp_range<-scale(sdat$pp_range)
sdat$ssalinity<-scale(sdat$salinity)
sdat$snitrate<-scale(sdat$nitrate)
sdat$sPAR<-scale(sdat$PAR)

## drop rows missing any model variable or response (required by na.action="na.fail" / dredge)
sdat <- sdat %>% filter(complete.cases(y, sTemp, snitrate, spp_range, sland_distance))
```

## Richness LMM and spatial diagnostics
Exploratory analyses — not manuscript figures or tables. Set eval=FALSE for faster knitting.
VIF for manyglm predictors: all < 3 (confirmed). Spatial weights (us.nb4/us.wt4) retained
for reference but not used in current analysis. LMM dredge confirms no random effect needed.
```{r stat_exploratory, eval=FALSE}
## VIF checks
HH::vif(xx = as.data.frame(sdat[ , c("slat","sTemp","sSST_range","snitrate","spp","spp_range","ssalinity","sland_distance")]))
HH::vif(xx = as.data.frame(sdat[ , c("sTemp","snitrate","spp_range","sland_distance")]))

## Richness distribution
x <- sdat$rich_rare
hist(x); hist(sqrt(x)); hist(log(x))

## Spatial weights (k=8 nearest neighbours) — built for potential SAR models
ssdat  <- sdat
coords <- cbind(ssdat$Longitude, ssdat$Latitude)
us.nb4 <- knn2nb(knearneigh(coords, k = 8))
us.wt4 <- nb2listw(us.nb4, style = "W")

## Richness LMM — model selection via dredge
lmer.mod.1 <- lmer(y ~ habitat + sTemp + snitrate + spp_range + sland_distance
                   + (1|season), data = sdat, na.action = "na.fail", REML = FALSE)
lmer.mod.2 <- lm(y ~ habitat + sTemp + snitrate + spp_range + sland_distance,
                 data = sdat, na.action = "na.fail")
AICs <- c(AIC(lmer.mod.1), AIC(lmer.mod.2)); AICs
# best model is without random factor

dred <- MuMIn::dredge(lmer.mod.2)
subset(dred, delta == 0)

lmer.mod <- lm(y ~ habitat + sTemp + snitrate + spp_range + sland_distance,
               data = sdat, na.action = "na.fail")
summary(lmer.mod)
MuMIn::r.squaredGLMM(lmer.mod)

## Residual diagnostics
mod <- lmer.mod
hist(resid(mod))
plot(fitted(mod), resid(mod)); abline(0, 0)
qqnorm(resid(mod)); qqline(resid(mod))
```


## Community matrix

```{r community_matrix}
## ---- presence/absence community matrix (samples × OTUs) --------------------
## Use combined-primer data; 1 = OTU detected in sample, 0 = absent.
## Presence/absence reduces the influence of highly variable read counts
## and is consistent with the Arctic paper (binomial manyglm).
comm_pa <- dat_all_filt_combine_prim %>%
  filter(type == "sample") %>%
  select(sample_id, lineage, percent_reads) %>%
  group_by(sample_id, lineage) %>%
  summarise(pres = as.integer(sum(percent_reads, na.rm = TRUE) > 0),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from  = lineage,
              values_from = pres,
              values_fill = 0L) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample_id")

## ---- align env data rows to community matrix rows --------------------------
## sdat was built in the stat chunk; subset to samples present in comm_pa.
env_mva <- sdat %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(as.character(sample_id) %in% rownames(comm_pa)) %>%
  arrange(match(as.character(sample_id), rownames(comm_pa))) %>%
  as.data.frame()

## reorder community matrix rows to match env_mva
comm_pa <- comm_pa[as.character(env_mva$sample_id), ]

## remove OTUs present in fewer than 5 samples (~6% occurrence; colSums >= 2
## is effectively no filter — all 493 taxa already pass it)
comm_pa <- comm_pa[, colSums(comm_pa) >= 5]

cat("Community matrix:", nrow(comm_pa), "samples ×", ncol(comm_pa), "OTUs\n")
```


## manyglm analysis

```{r manyglm_fit}
## ---- set reference level: Coral ---------------------------------------------
## Explicit relevel so habitatMangrove = Mangrove vs Coral,
## habitatSeagrass = Seagrass vs Coral in all model output.
env_mva$habitat <- relevel(factor(env_mva$habitat), ref = "Coral")

## ---- model 1: Coral reference (for Table 1 + Mangrove/Seagrass vs Coral) ---
mva_dat <- mvabund(comm_pa)

mva_mod <- manyglm(
  mva_dat ~ habitat + sTemp + snitrate + spp_range + sland_distance,
  data   = env_mva,
  family = binomial("cloglog"),
  nCore  = 4
)
summary(mva_mod)
## mva_aov: multivariate only — fast, used for Table 1.
## nBoot=999 for publication; 99 for dev runs.
mva_aov <- anova(mva_mod,
                 resamp   = "pit.trap",
                 test     = "score",
                 cor.type = "shrink",
                 nBoot    = 999,
                 p.uni    = "none")

## anova for model 1: gives per-dummy p-values (habitatMangrove, habitatSeagrass)
## correctly for this model. summary is NOT used here — it applies a more
## conservative cross-coefficient adjustment that washes out significance.
mva_aov_uni <- anova(mva_mod,
                     resamp   = "pit.trap",
                     test     = "score",
                     cor.type = "shrink",
                     nBoot    = 999,
                     p.uni    = "adjusted")

## ---- model 2: rebuild everything from scratch with Mangrove as reference ----
## Completely independent objects (comm_pa2, env_mva2, mva_dat2) to eliminate
## any state carried over from model 1.
comm_pa2 <- dat_all_filt_combine_prim %>%
  filter(type == "sample") %>%
  select(sample_id, lineage, percent_reads) %>%
  group_by(sample_id, lineage) %>%
  summarise(pres = as.integer(sum(percent_reads, na.rm = TRUE) > 0),
            .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from  = lineage,
              values_from = pres,
              values_fill = 0L) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample_id")

env_mva2 <- sdat %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  filter(as.character(sample_id) %in% rownames(comm_pa2)) %>%
  arrange(match(as.character(sample_id), rownames(comm_pa2))) %>%
  as.data.frame()

comm_pa2 <- comm_pa2[as.character(env_mva2$sample_id), ]
comm_pa2 <- comm_pa2[, colSums(comm_pa2) >= 5]

env_mva2$habitat <- relevel(factor(env_mva2$habitat), ref = "Mangrove")

mva_dat2 <- mvabund(comm_pa2)

mva_mod2 <- manyglm(
  mva_dat2 ~ habitat + sTemp + snitrate + spp_range + sland_distance,
  data   = env_mva2,
  family = binomial("cloglog")
)

mva_aov_uni2 <- anova(mva_mod2,
                      resamp   = "pit.trap",
                      test     = "score",
                      cor.type = "shrink",
                      nBoot    = 999,
                      p.uni    = "adjusted")

```

```{r table1_manyglm}
## Column names from mvabund anova table: Res.Df, Df.diff, score, Pr(>score)
tab1_raw <- as.data.frame(mva_aov$table) %>%
  rownames_to_column("variable") %>%
  filter(variable != "(Intercept)") %>%
  rename(
    `Res. DF`  = Res.Df,
    `d.f.`     = Df.diff,
```

## Fig 4 — Multivariate GLM plot

```{r multivar_plot_ggplot, warning=FALSE}
t         <- mva_mod
t.an      <- mva_aov_uni
taxa_file <- dat_all_filt_combine_prim

## variable display order and axis labels
## Two habitat contrasts from model 1 (Coral ref) + SvM from model 2 (Mangrove ref).
var_order <- c("habitatMangrove", "habitatSeagrass", "SvM",
               "sTemp", "snitrate", "spp_range", "sland_distance")
x_labels  <- c("Mangrove vs Coral", "Seagrass vs Coral", "Seagrass vs Mangrove",
               "SST mean", "Nitrate", "Prim. prod. range", "Dist. to shore")

## p_min_val is auto-calculated below to display ~15 taxa
num_clust  <- 5            # hierarchical clusters for y-axis colour grouping
ccll       <- c(wesanderson::wes_palette("Moonrise2", n = 2), "black")  # matches Arctic
pal3       <- wesanderson::wes_palette("Zissou1", 3, type = "continuous")  # dot colours
col_sig    <- c("not significant" = "grey85", "significant" = "grey40")  # explicit mapping

## ── Extract model 1 components ───────────────────────────────────────────────
## anova$uni.test: rows = predictors, cols = taxa — transpose to get rows = taxa
t.coef <- coef(t)
t.ts   <- t(t.an$uni.test)   # rows = taxa, cols = predictors
t.p    <- t(t.an$uni.p)

## test statistic (long format)
mult_dat <- data.frame(t.ts) %>%
  rownames_to_column("lineage") %>%
  select(-any_of(c("X.Intercept.", "X.Intercept"))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-lineage, names_to = "variable", values_to = "test_stat")

## p-value (long)
mult_dat_p <- data.frame(t.p) %>%
  rownames_to_column("lineage") %>%
  select(-any_of(c("X.Intercept.", "X.Intercept"))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-lineage, names_to = "variable", values_to = "p.value")

## coefficient (long)
mult_dat_c <- data.frame(t(t.coef)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("lineage") %>%
  select(-any_of(c("X.Intercept.", "X.Intercept"))) %>%
  pivot_longer(-lineage, names_to = "variable", values_to = "coef")

## ── Expand combined "habitat" anova row into two named contrast rows ----------
## anova tests habitat as a 2-df term; duplicate that row so both contrasts
## appear as columns in the plot. Coefficient direction comes from coef() below.
expand_hab <- function(df) {
  hab <- df %>% filter(variable == "habitat")
  bind_rows(
    df %>% filter(variable != "habitat"),
    hab %>% mutate(variable = "habitatMangrove"),
    hab %>% mutate(variable = "habitatSeagrass")
  )
}
mult_dat   <- expand_hab(mult_dat)
mult_dat_p <- expand_hab(mult_dat_p)

## ── Add Seagrass vs Mangrove from model 2 anova ──────────────────────────────
## Tile significance: combined 2-df habitat row from mva_aov_uni2 (same test
## as MvC/SvC but from model 2). Coefficient direction: habitatSeagrass in
## model 2 = Seagrass vs Mangrove contrast (Mangrove is reference).
svM_ts <- data.frame(t(mva_aov_uni2$uni.test)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("lineage") %>%
  select(lineage, test_stat = habitat) %>%
  mutate(variable = "SvM") %>%
  filter(lineage %in% mult_dat$lineage)

svM_p <- data.frame(t(mva_aov_uni2$uni.p)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("lineage") %>%
  select(lineage, p.value = habitat) %>%
  mutate(variable = "SvM") %>%
  filter(lineage %in% mult_dat$lineage)

svM_c <- data.frame(t(coef(mva_mod2))) %>%
  rownames_to_column("lineage") %>%
  select(lineage, coef = habitatSeagrass) %>%
  mutate(variable = "SvM") %>%
  filter(lineage %in% mult_dat$lineage)

mult_dat   <- bind_rows(mult_dat,   svM_ts)
mult_dat_p <- bind_rows(mult_dat_p, svM_p)
mult_dat_c <- bind_rows(mult_dat_c, svM_c)
## ── Auto-select p_min_val to display ~n_target taxa --------------------------
n_target  <- 15
p_min_val <- mult_dat_p %>%
  group_by(lineage) %>%
  summarise(min_p = min(p.value, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(min_p) %>%
  slice(min(n_target, n())) %>%
  pull(min_p)
cat("p_min_val =", round(p_min_val, 4), "| taxa displayed:", n_target, "\n")

## join; keep taxa with at least one predictor at p ≤ p_min_val
mult_dat2 <- mult_dat %>%
  left_join(mult_dat_p, by = c("lineage", "variable")) %>%
  left_join(mult_dat_c, by = c("lineage", "variable")) %>%
  group_by(lineage) %>%
  filter(any(p.value <= p_min_val)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    p_val_col = if_else(p.value <= 0.05, "significant", "not significant"),
    coef_log  = if_else(coef >= 0, log(coef + 1), -log(abs(coef) + 1))
  )

## ── Hierarchical clustering of taxa by coefficient ───────────────────────────
## Cluster on continuous predictors only — habitat dummies excluded as they
## represent contrasts vs reference level, not a continuous gradient.
cont_pred <- c("sTemp", "snitrate", "spp_range", "sland_distance")
clus <- t(t.coef)[, cont_pred, drop = FALSE]
clus <- clus[match(unique(mult_dat2$lineage), rownames(clus)), , drop = FALSE]

hc      <- hclust(sqrt(dist(clus)))
plot(hc, main = "Taxa dendrogram (coefficient distances)")
rect.hclust(hc, k = num_clust)

clgroup <- data.frame(group = cutree(hc, k = num_clust)) %>%
  rownames_to_column("lineage")
ccc     <- data.frame(group = seq_len(num_clust),
                      color = rep(ccll, length.out = num_clust))

clustorder <- clgroup %>%
  left_join(ccc, by = "group") %>%
  mutate(taxa_cluster_arrange = as.integer(
    factor(lineage, levels = hc$labels[hc$order])
  ))

## ── Y-axis labels: Phylum;Order;Family;Genus ─────────────────────────────────
## Row names in t.p are R-safe lineage strings (;→. space→. -→.).
## Create matching 'lineage_stat' from the original lineage column to join.
rn <- data.frame(lineage_stat = rownames(t.p))

y_labels_make <- taxa_file %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(lineage:Species) %>%
  distinct(lineage, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(lineage_stat = make.names(lineage)) %>%
  inner_join(rn, by = "lineage_stat") %>%
  unite(y_labels, Phylum:Genus, sep = ";", remove = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(y_labels = gsub("Eukaryota", "Unclassified", y_labels),
         y_labels = gsub("NA",        "Unclassified", y_labels))

y_labels <- clustorder %>%
  left_join(y_labels_make, by = c("lineage" = "lineage_stat")) %>%
  arrange(taxa_cluster_arrange) %>%
  mutate(y_labels = if_else(is.na(y_labels), lineage, y_labels))

## ── Build plotting data ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
## Convert variable to factor and drop rows not in var_order (e.g. combined
## 'habitat' term if anova didn't expand dummies), then derive xx/yy from
## factor integers — robust to any number of variables per taxon.
mult_dat3 <- mult_dat2 %>%
  left_join(clustorder, by = "lineage") %>%
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = var_order)) %>%
  filter(!is.na(variable)) %>%
  arrange(taxa_cluster_arrange, variable) %>%
  mutate(
    xx = as.integer(variable),
    yy = as.integer(factor(lineage, levels = unique(lineage)))
  )

cat("Variables in plot:", paste(sort(unique(as.character(mult_dat3$variable))), collapse=", "), "\n")
cat("Taxa in plot:", n_distinct(mult_dat3$lineage), "\n")

## ── Plot ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
upper_coef <- 0.9
lower_coef <- -upper_coef
dd         <- 2   # divisor for intermediate legend breaks

mult_plot <- ggplot(mult_dat3, aes(xx, yy)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = p_val_col), colour = "grey50") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = col_sig, na.value = "grey85") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = coef_log, size = test_stat)) +
  scale_color_gradientn(
    name   = "Coefficient",
    colors = pal3,
    space  = "Lab",
    values = scales::rescale(c(lower_coef * 1.1, lower_coef / 9, 0,
                               upper_coef / 9,   upper_coef * 1.1)),
    limits = c(lower_coef * 1.1, upper_coef * 1.1),
    breaks = c(lower_coef, lower_coef / dd, 0, upper_coef / dd, upper_coef),
    labels = round(c(-(exp(abs(lower_coef)) - 1),
                     -(exp(abs(lower_coef / dd)) - 1),
                     0,
                      (exp(upper_coef / dd) - 1),
                      (exp(upper_coef) - 1)), 1),
    oob    = scales::squish
  ) +
  scale_size(name = "Score stat") +
  scale_x_continuous(name = NULL,
                     breaks = seq_along(levels(mult_dat3$variable)),
                     labels = x_labels[seq_along(levels(mult_dat3$variable))],
                     guide  = guide_axis(angle = 45)) +
  scale_y_continuous(name = NULL,
                     breaks = seq_along(y_labels$y_labels),
                     labels = y_labels$y_labels,
                     expand = expansion(add = 0.5)) +
  guides(fill = "none") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
    axis.text.y  = element_text(colour = y_labels$color),
    axis.ticks   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid   = element_blank()
  )

mult_plot

ggsave(mult_plot,
       file   = paste0(dir, plot_file, "/Fig4_multvar_taxa_presabs.tiff"),
       width  = 20, height = 25, units = "cm", dpi = "print")
```


## NMDS and ordisurf GAMs

```{r nmds_gam}
## ---- NMDS on Bray-Curtis (log-transformed percent reads) -------------------
comm_pct <- dat_all_filt_combine_prim %>%
  filter(type == "sample") %>%
  select(sample_id, lineage, percent_reads) %>%
  group_by(sample_id, lineage) %>%
  summarise(percent_reads = sum(percent_reads, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from  = lineage,
              values_from = percent_reads,
              values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample_id")

comm_pct <- comm_pct[as.character(env_mva$sample_id), ]
comm_pct <- comm_pct[, colSums(comm_pct > 0) >= 2]

## log(x+1) transformation then Bray-Curtis (as in Arctic paper)
nmds_res <- metaMDS(log1p(comm_pct),
                    distance      = "bray",
                    trymax        = 100,
                    autotransform = FALSE,
                    trace         = FALSE)

cat("NMDS stress:", round(nmds_res$stress, 3), "\n")
## Stress < 0.1 = good; 0.1-0.2 = fair; > 0.2 = poor

## ---- individual GAMs via ordisurf ------------------------------------------
## All continuous env variables run individually; habitat excluded (categorical,
## already in manyglm). Raw (unscaled) values used; ordisurf scales internally.
## Variables removed from manyglm due to covariance are included here to show
## non-linear gradients alongside the manyglm set.
env_vars_gam <- list(
  "Latitude"                     = env_mva$lat,
  "SST (mean)"                   = env_mva$sst_mean,
  "SST (range)"                  = env_mva$SST_range,
  "Nitrate"                      = env_mva$nitrate,
  "Primary productivity (mean)"  = env_mva$pp_mean,
  "Primary productivity (range)" = env_mva$pp_range,
  "Salinity"                     = env_mva$salinity,
  "Distance to shore"            = env_mva$land_distance
)

ordisurf_fits <- list()

tab2_raw <- lapply(names(env_vars_gam), function(v) {
  vals <- env_vars_gam[[v]]
  if (sum(!is.na(vals)) < 5) return(NULL)
  surf <- ordisurf(nmds_res, vals, plot = FALSE, bs = "tp")
  ordisurf_fits[[v]] <<- surf  # <<- needed: lapply creates child env; list lives in parent
  s  <- summary(surf)
  st <- s$s.table
  data.frame(
    variable           = v,
    Est.DF             = round(st[1, "edf"],    2),
    Ref.DF             = round(st[1, "Ref.df"], 2),
    F.value            = round(st[1, "F"],      2),
    p.value            = round(st[1, "p-value"],4),
    deviance_explained = round(s$dev.expl * 100, 1),
    stringsAsFactors   = FALSE
  )
}) %>% bind_rows()
```
