## Build L, R, Q matrices

```{r fc_matrices}
## ---- 1. Build the L matrix (sites × species, percent_reads) ----------------
L_long <- dat_all_filt_combine_prim %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  select(sample_id, lineage, percent_reads) %>%
  group_by(sample_id, lineage) %>%
  summarise(percent_reads = sum(percent_reads), .groups = "drop")

L_wide <- L_long %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = lineage, values_from = percent_reads, values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample_id")

## ---- 2. Build the R matrix (sites × env variables) -------------------------
## Matches manyglm predictors: 4 continuous env vars + habitat (categorical).
## dudi.hillsmith() handles mixed continuous/factor variables.
## fourthcorner uses D2 statistic for continuous R × Q pairs and
## G statistic (chi-square-like) for categorical R (habitat) × Q pairs.
env_vars <- c("sst_mean", "nitrate", "pp_range", "land_distance")

env_sub <- env %>%
  rename_all(tolower) %>%
  filter(sample_id %in% rownames(L_wide)) %>%
  arrange(match(sample_id, rownames(L_wide)))

R_mat <- env_sub %>%
  select(all_of(tolower(env_vars))) %>%
  mutate(across(everything(), ~as.numeric(scale(.)))) %>%
  as.data.frame()
rownames(R_mat) <- env_sub$sample_id

## Add habitat as categorical variable
hab_lookup   <- dat_all_filt_combine_prim %>% distinct(sample_id, habitat)
R_mat$habitat <- factor(
  hab_lookup$habitat[match(rownames(R_mat), hab_lookup$sample_id)]
)

L_wide <- L_wide[rownames(R_mat), ]

## ---- 3. Build the Q matrix (species × traits) ------------------------------
## Lineage prefix mismatch: L_wide uses "Eukaryota;..." but trait_dat starts at
## kingdom — strip prefix for matching, restore afterwards (same as tiding join).
lwide_stripped <- sub("^[^;]+;", "", colnames(L_wide))

## trait_dat is pre-cleaned (zone renamed from zone...16, recoding applied)
Q_mat <- trait_dat %>%
  distinct(lineage, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(lineage %in% lwide_stripped) %>%
  select(lineage, zone, trophic.level, as_catagory,
         planktonic.larval.form, mobility) %>%
  column_to_rownames("lineage") %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor)) %>%
  as.data.frame()

## Align species: intersect on stripped names, restore full-prefix rownames.
shared_stripped <- intersect(lwide_stripped, rownames(Q_mat))
keep_cols       <- colnames(L_wide)[lwide_stripped %in% shared_stripped]
L_wide          <- L_wide[, keep_cols, drop = FALSE]
rownames(Q_mat) <- keep_cols[match(rownames(Q_mat),
                                   sub("^[^;]+;", "", keep_cols))]
Q_mat           <- Q_mat[colnames(L_wide), , drop = FALSE]

## Drop species with any remaining NA trait values and re-align L_wide.
complete_sp <- rownames(Q_mat)[complete.cases(Q_mat)]
Q_mat  <- Q_mat[complete_sp, , drop = FALSE]
L_wide <- L_wide[, complete_sp, drop = FALSE]
cat("Species retained after NA filter:", nrow(Q_mat), "\n")
```


## Trait diagnostics
Run after `fc_matrices` to verify category counts before the permutation test.
```{r trait_diagnostics}
## ── 1. Species counts at each filtering step ──────────────────────────────────
n_total_sp <- length(lwide_stripped)
n_matched  <- length(shared_stripped)
n_complete <- nrow(Q_mat)

step_df <- data.frame(
  Step = c("Species in community (L_wide)",
           "Matched to trait file",
           "  Not matched (absent from trait file)",
           "Retained — complete trait data",
           "  Dropped — ≥ 1 trait value missing"),
  N    = c(n_total_sp, n_matched, n_total_sp - n_matched,
           n_complete,  n_matched  - n_complete)
)
kable(step_df, col.names = c("Step", "N species"), format = "html",
      caption = "Species retained at each filtering step for fourth-corner / RLQ") %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

## ── 2. Community read coverage ────────────────────────────────────────────────
reads_total    <- sum(L_long$percent_reads[
                    L_long$sample_id %in% rownames(L_wide)])
reads_retained <- sum(L_wide)
cat(sprintf(
  "\nRead coverage: retained species account for %.1f%% of reads in analysed samples.\n\n",
  100 * reads_retained / reads_total
))

## ── 3. Missing data by trait (among matched species, before NA filter) ─────────
Q_all_matched <- trait_dat %>%
  distinct(lineage, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  filter(lineage %in% shared_stripped) %>%
  select(zone, trophic.level, as_catagory,
         planktonic.larval.form, mobility)

miss_df <- data.frame(
  Trait       = colnames(Q_all_matched),
  Present     = sapply(Q_all_matched, function(x) sum(!is.na(x))),
  Missing     = sapply(Q_all_matched, function(x) sum( is.na(x))),
  Pct_missing = round(100 * sapply(Q_all_matched, function(x) mean(is.na(x))), 1)
)
kable(miss_df, row.names = FALSE, format = "html",
      col.names = c("Trait", "Present", "Missing", "% missing"),
      caption = paste("Missing trait data among", n_matched,
                      "species matched to trait file")) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE)

## ── 4. Category counts per trait in Q_mat (species used in analysis) ──────────
count_list <- lapply(colnames(Q_mat), function(tr) {
  col <- Q_mat[[tr]]
  if (is.factor(col)) {
    tbl <- sort(table(col), decreasing = TRUE)
    data.frame(Trait    = tr,
               Category = names(tbl),
               N        = as.integer(tbl),
               Flag     = ifelse(as.integer(tbl) < 5, "< 5 — consider merging", ""),
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  } else {
    data.frame(Trait    = tr,
               Category = sprintf("continuous  [%.2f – %.2f]",
                                  min(col, na.rm = TRUE), max(col, na.rm = TRUE)),
               N        = sum(!is.na(col)),
               Flag     = "",
               stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }
})
count_df <- bind_rows(count_list)
kable(count_df, row.names = FALSE, format = "html",
      col.names = c("Trait", "Category", "N species", "Flag"),
      caption = paste("Trait category counts in Q_mat (", nrow(Q_mat),
                      "species). Yellow = < 5 species; consider merging.")) %>%
  kable_styling(full_width = FALSE) %>%
  row_spec(which(count_df$Flag != ""), background = "#fff3cd")

## ── 5. Cross-tabulations of all factor trait pairs ────────────────────────────
cat("\n=== Cross-tabulations of factor trait pairs (flag cells < 3 species) ===\n\n")
factor_traits <- names(which(sapply(Q_mat, is.factor)))
if (length(factor_traits) >= 2) {
  for (pair in combn(factor_traits, 2, simplify = FALSE)) {
    ct <- table(Q_mat[[pair[1]]], Q_mat[[pair[2]]], dnn = pair)
    cat(pair[1], "×", pair[2], ":\n")
    print(ct)
    if (any(ct > 0 & ct < 3))
      cat("  *** cells with 1–2 species — consider merging levels ***\n")
    cat("\n")
  }
}
```


## Fourth corner fit
Fourth-corner test (Dray & Legendre 2008, Ecology 89:3400–3412). `modeltype=6`
combined permutation test; `p.adjust.method="none"` correct — the combined
permutation IS the multiple-testing correction. Display threshold α = 0.2.
Run this chunk before `rlq_biplot` and `fourth_corner_plot`.

```{r fc_fit}
fc_res <- fourthcorner(
  tabR               = R_mat,
  tabL               = L_wide,
  tabQ               = Q_mat,
  modeltype          = 6,
  p.adjust.method.D  = "none",
  p.adjust.method.G  = "none",
  nrepet             = 9999
)
print(fc_res)

nR <- length(fc_res$colnames.R)   # includes expanded habitat levels
nQ <- length(fc_res$colnames.Q)

## D2 and D statistics (for continuous R rows)
d2_mat   <- matrix(fc_res$tabD2$obs,    nrow = nR, ncol = nQ,
                   dimnames = list(fc_res$colnames.R, fc_res$colnames.Q))
d_mat    <- matrix(fc_res$tabD$obs,     nrow = nR, ncol = nQ,
                   dimnames = list(fc_res$colnames.R, fc_res$colnames.Q))

## G statistic (for categorical R rows — habitat levels)
g_mat    <- matrix(fc_res$tabG$obs,    nrow = nR, ncol = nQ,
                   dimnames = list(fc_res$colnames.R, fc_res$colnames.Q))

## Combined p-value matrix: D2 p-values for continuous rows, G p-values for habitat rows.
## fc_res$assignR maps each expanded colnames.R entry to its original variable (1-indexed).
## fc_res$indexR gives the type (1 = continuous, 2 = categorical) per original variable.
row_type  <- fc_res$indexR[fc_res$assignR]   # type per expanded R row
pval_d2   <- matrix(fc_res$tabD2$pvalue, nrow = nR, ncol = nQ,
                    dimnames = list(fc_res$colnames.R, fc_res$colnames.Q))
pval_g    <- matrix(fc_res$tabG$pvalue,  nrow = nR, ncol = nQ,
                    dimnames = list(fc_res$colnames.R, fc_res$colnames.Q))
pval_mat  <- pval_d2
pval_mat[row_type == 2, ] <- pval_g[row_type == 2, ]   # habitat rows use G p-values

cat("R variable types (1=continuous, 2=categorical):\n")
print(data.frame(var = fc_res$colnames.R, type = row_type))
cat("Row sums d2_mat:", paste(round(rowSums(d2_mat), 3), collapse = ", "), "\n")
```


## RLQ biplot and habitat ordination
RLQ site scores coloured by habitat with 75% data ellipses (`type = "norm"`
= data ellipse unaffected by sample size, unlike CI ellipses which inflate
with small n). Trait arrows filtered to fourth-corner significant levels
(p ≤ 0.2 from fc_fit); all env variable arrows retained (only 4 total).

```{r rlq_biplot}
## ---- RLQ ordination ---------------------------------------------------------
afcL    <- dudi.coa(L_wide, scannf = FALSE, nf = 2)
acpR    <- dudi.hillsmith(R_mat, row.w = afcL$lw, scannf = FALSE, nf = 2)
acpQ    <- dudi.hillsmith(Q_mat, row.w = afcL$cw, scannf = FALSE, nf = 2)
rlq_res <- rlq(acpR, afcL, acpQ, scannf = FALSE, nf = 2)
summary(rlq_res)

tiff(paste0(dir, plot_file, "/RLQ_biplot_baseR.tiff"),
     width = 18, height = 15, units = "cm", res = 300)
plot(rlq_res)
dev.off()

## ---- Extract RLQ scores -----------------------------------------------------
rlq_sites <- as.data.frame(rlq_res$lR) %>%
  rownames_to_column("sample_id") %>%
  rename(RLQ1 = 2, RLQ2 = 3) %>%
  left_join(distinct(plot_dat_phylum, sample_id, habitat), by = "sample_id") %>%
  mutate(habitat = factor(habitat, levels = names(hab_cols)))

rlq_env <- as.data.frame(rlq_res$l1) %>%
  rownames_to_column("var") %>%
  rename(RLQ1 = 2, RLQ2 = 3)

rlq_traits_all <- as.data.frame(rlq_res$c1) %>%
  rownames_to_column("trait") %>%
  rename(RLQ1 = 2, RLQ2 = 3)

## ---- Filter trait arrows to fourth-corner significant levels ----------------
## sig_fc_levels: trait levels where min p across env vars ≤ 0.2
sig_fc_levels <- fc_res$colnames.Q[apply(pval_mat, 2, min) <= 0.2]

rlq_traits_sig <- rlq_traits_all %>%
  filter(trait %in% sig_fc_levels) %>%
  mutate(label = sub("^[^.]+\\.", "", trait))  # strip trait-name prefix

## ---- Arrow scaling ----------------------------------------------------------
## Stretch arrows to ~75% of the site cloud radius
site_radius <- max(sqrt(rlq_sites$RLQ1^2 + rlq_sites$RLQ2^2), na.rm = TRUE)
env_radius  <- max(sqrt(rlq_env$RLQ1^2   + rlq_env$RLQ2^2),   na.rm = TRUE)
arr_mul     <- 0.75 * site_radius / env_radius

env_lbl_arr <- c(sst_mean      = "SST mean",
                 nitrate       = "Nitrate",
                 pp_range      = "PP range",
                 land_distance = "Dist. shore")

rlq_env_plot <- rlq_env %>%
  mutate(xend  = RLQ1 * arr_mul,  yend  = RLQ2 * arr_mul,
         lbl_x = RLQ1 * arr_mul * 1.18, lbl_y = RLQ2 * arr_mul * 1.18,
         label = unname(env_lbl_arr[var]))

## Scale trait arrows by the same factor
rlq_traits_plot <- rlq_traits_sig %>%
  mutate(xend  = RLQ1 * arr_mul,  yend  = RLQ2 * arr_mul,
         lbl_x = RLQ1 * arr_mul * 1.18, lbl_y = RLQ2 * arr_mul * 1.18)

## ---- Plot -------------------------------------------------------------------
## type = "norm" = data ellipse (spread of points, unaffected by n).
## level = 0.75 keeps ellipses compact; raise/lower to taste.
fig_rlq <- ggplot(rlq_sites, aes(RLQ1, RLQ2)) +
  stat_ellipse(aes(fill = habitat, colour = habitat),
               type = "norm", level = 0.75, geom = "polygon",
               alpha = 0.12, linewidth = 1.1, linetype = "solid") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = habitat, shape = habitat),
             size = 2.2, alpha = 0.9) +
  scale_fill_manual(values   = hab_cols, name = "Habitat") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = hab_cols, name = "Habitat") +
  scale_shape_manual(values  = c(16, 17, 15), name = "Habitat") +
  ## Env arrows (blue)
  geom_segment(data = rlq_env_plot,
               aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = xend, yend = yend),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.18, "cm"), type = "closed"),
               colour = "#2166AC", linewidth = 0.9, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_text(data = rlq_env_plot,
            aes(x = lbl_x, y = lbl_y, label = label),
            colour = "#2166AC", size = 3.0, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  ## Trait arrows — fourth-corner significant only (red dashed)
  geom_segment(data = rlq_traits_plot,
               aes(x = 0, y = 0, xend = xend, yend = yend),
               arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.18, "cm"), type = "closed"),
               colour = "#C0392B", linewidth = 0.7, linetype = "dashed",
               inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_text(data = rlq_traits_plot,
            aes(x = lbl_x, y = lbl_y, label = label),
            colour = "#C0392B", size = 2.8, inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dotted", colour = "grey60") +
  theme_bw(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.border    = element_rect(colour = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.8),
        legend.position = "right") +
  labs(x = "RLQ axis 1", y = "RLQ axis 2")

fig_rlq

ggsave(paste0(dir, plot_file, "/Fig_RLQ_biplot.tiff"),
       fig_rlq, width = 18, height = 14, units = "cm", dpi = 300)
```

## Fourth corner plot
Tile + dot plot: env variables on x-axis, trait categories on y-axis grouped
into trait facets. Tile shading = significance (α = 0.2); dot colour =
direction (D stat, Zissou1 blue→red); dot size = strength (√D²).

```{r fourth_corner_plot}
## Axis labels: continuous env vars + habitat levels (expanded from factor)
## fc_res$colnames.R now includes "habitat.Coral", "habitat.Mangrove", etc.
env_lbl_cont <- c(sst_mean      = "SST (mean)",
                  nitrate       = "Nitrate",
                  pp_range      = "Prim. prod. (range)",
                  land_distance = "Dist. to shore")

## Build label for every expanded R variable:
## continuous vars get their nice name; habitat levels strip the "habitat." prefix
env_row_lbl <- setNames(
  ifelse(fc_res$colnames.R %in% names(env_lbl_cont),
         unname(env_lbl_cont[fc_res$colnames.R]),
         sub("^[^.]+\\.", "", fc_res$colnames.R)),
  fc_res$colnames.R
)

clean_level     <- sub("^[^.]+\\.", "", fc_res$colnames.Q)
trait_group     <- fc_res$varnames.Q[fc_res$assignQ]
trait_group_lbl <- c(zone                   = "Zone",
                     trophic.level          = "Trophic level",
                     as_catagory            = "Body size",
                     planktonic.larval.form = "Planktonic larval",
                     mobility               = "Mobility")

to_long_fc <- function(mat, val) {
  as.data.frame(mat) %>%
    rownames_to_column("env") %>%
    pivot_longer(-env, names_to = "trait_level", values_to = val)
}

## row_type_long: 1 = continuous, 2 = categorical (habitat); drives dot display.
row_type_vec <- setNames(row_type, fc_res$colnames.R)

fc_long <- to_long_fc(d2_mat, "D2") %>%
  left_join(to_long_fc(pval_mat, "p_value"), by = c("env", "trait_level")) %>%
  left_join(to_long_fc(d_mat,   "D_stat"),  by = c("env", "trait_level")) %>%
  left_join(to_long_fc(g_mat,   "G_stat"),  by = c("env", "trait_level")) %>%
  mutate(
    r_type      = unname(row_type_vec[env]),
    sig_tile    = if_else(p_value <= 0.2, "significant", "not significant"),
    ## Dot size: √D2 for continuous rows, √G for habitat rows
    dot_size    = if_else(r_type == 1, sqrt(pmax(D2, 0)), sqrt(pmax(G_stat, 0))),
    D_stat_plot = D2,      ## tabD2 is signed (-0.15 to +18.6); tabD is unsigned magnitude
    env_label   = unname(env_row_lbl[env]),
    level_clean = clean_level[match(trait_level, fc_res$colnames.Q)],
    trait_grp   = trait_group[match(trait_level, fc_res$colnames.Q)],
    trait_grp_f = factor(unname(trait_group_lbl[trait_grp]),
                         levels = unname(trait_group_lbl[fc_res$varnames.Q])),
    ## Habitat columns first (matching manyglm order), then continuous env vars
    env_f       = factor(env_label,
                         levels = unname(env_row_lbl[c(
                           names(row_type_vec)[row_type_vec == 2],
                           names(row_type_vec)[row_type_vec == 1]
                         )])),
    level_f     = factor(level_clean, levels = unique(clean_level))
  )

col_sig <- c("not significant" = "grey85", "significant" = "grey40")

## Symmetric limits force the legend to span full blue→red even though all
## observed D values are positive (data appears yellow→red in the plot).
## This matches Fig 4's palette and makes clear negative relationships are possible.
max_d <- max(abs(fc_long$D_stat_plot), na.rm = TRUE)

fc_gg <- ggplot(fc_long, aes(env_f, level_f)) +
  facet_grid(trait_grp_f ~ ., scales = "free_y", space = "free_y", switch = "y") +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = sig_tile), colour = "grey50",
            width = 0.92, height = 0.92) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = col_sig, name = NULL) +
  ## All rows (continuous + habitat): colour = D stat, size = strength
  geom_point(aes(colour = D_stat_plot, size = dot_size)) +
  scale_colour_gradient2(
    name     = "Direction\n(D stat)",
    low      = pal3[1], mid = pal3[2], high = pal3[3],
    midpoint = 0,
    limits   = c(-max_d, max_d)
  ) +
  scale_size_continuous(name = "Strength", range = c(1, 7)) +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(
    strip.text.y.left = element_text(size = 9, face = "bold", angle = 0),
    strip.placement   = "outside",
    axis.text.x       = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1, size = 10),
    axis.text.y       = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.ticks        = element_blank(),
    panel.grid        = element_blank(),
    legend.position   = "right"
  ) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL)

fc_gg

ggsave(paste0(dir, plot_file, "/Fig6_fourth_corner.tiff"),
       fc_gg, width = 16, height = 20, units = "cm", dpi = 300)
```




## Distance decay
Bray-Curtis dissimilarity vs. through-water geographic distance (km).

Run `through_water_dist` once to download bathymetry and compute the distance
matrix, then set that chunk to `eval=FALSE` for subsequent knits.

```{r through_water_dist, eval=FALSE}
## Downloads NOAA ETOPO1 bathymetry for the Red Sea and computes pairwise
## through-water distances between all sample sites. Land cells act as barriers
## so distances are routed through ocean only (unlike Haversine straight-line).
## Saves through_water_dist_km.csv; re-run only if sample locations change.
library(marmap)
library(terra)

## All sample locations before otu filtering
pts_all <- dat_all_filt_combine_prim %>%
  filter(type == "sample") %>%
  distinct(sample_id, lon, lat)

## Download ETOPO1 at 1-arc-minute resolution (~1.85 km); cached as .csv in dir
bat <- marmap::getNOAA.bathy(
  lon1 = 31, lon2 = 45, lat1 = 11, lat2 = 31,
  resolution = 1,
  keep = TRUE,
  path = dir
)

## Convert to terra SpatRaster (marmap → raster → terra)
bat_rast <- terra::rast(marmap::as.raster(bat))

## Water mask: ocean (depth < 0) = 1; land (depth ≥ 0) = NA (barrier)
water_rast <- bat_rast
water_rast[bat_rast >= 0] <- NA
water_rast[!is.na(water_rast)] <- 1

## Dilate water mask by 1 cell (~1.85 km) so coastal sample points that fall
## just inside the land boundary of the raster are treated as water.
water_rast <- terra::focal(water_rast, w = 3, fun = "max", na.rm = TRUE,
                           na.policy = "omit")
water_rast[!is.na(water_rast)] <- 1

## SpatVector of sample points for extraction
pts_vect <- terra::vect(pts_all, geom = c("lon", "lat"), crs = "EPSG:4326")
n <- nrow(pts_all)

## Build symmetric distance matrix; gridDist routes through water only
tw_mat <- matrix(NA_real_, n, n,
                 dimnames = list(pts_all$sample_id, pts_all$sample_id))
diag(tw_mat) <- 0

for (i in seq_len(n)) {
  tmp  <- water_rast
  cell <- terra::cellFromXY(tmp, cbind(pts_all$lon[i], pts_all$lat[i]))
  tmp[cell] <- 2                        # mark focal site as target
  d <- terra::gridDist(tmp, target = 2) / 1000   # metres → km
  tw_mat[i, ] <- terra::extract(d, pts_vect)[, 2]
}

write.csv(tw_mat, paste0(dir, "through_water_dist_km.csv"), row.names = TRUE)
cat("Saved:", n, "×", n, "through-water distance matrix\n")
```

```{r dist_decay}
## ---- helper: dist object → data frame --------------------------------------
dist2df <- function(inDist) {
  A <- attr(inDist, "Size")
  B <- if (is.null(attr(inDist, "Labels"))) sequence(A) else attr(inDist, "Labels")
  if (isTRUE(attr(inDist, "Diag")))  attr(inDist, "Diag")  <- FALSE
  if (isTRUE(attr(inDist, "Upper"))) attr(inDist, "Upper") <- FALSE
  data.frame(
    row   = B[unlist(lapply(sequence(A)[-1], function(x) x:A))],
    col   = rep(B[-length(B)], (length(B) - 1):1),
    value = as.vector(inDist)
  )
}

## ---- OTU-style wide table (samples × taxa) ----------------------------------
min_samp_occur <- 2   # drop taxa present in fewer than this many samples
otu_wide <- dat_all_filt_combine_prim %>%
  filter(type == "sample") %>%
  select(sample_id, lineage, percent_reads) %>%
  group_by(sample_id, lineage) %>%
  summarise(percent_reads = sum(percent_reads), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = lineage, values_from = percent_reads, values_fill = 0) %>%
  column_to_rownames("sample_id")

cc       <- apply(otu_wide, 2, function(x) sum(x > 0))
otu_wide <- otu_wide[, cc >= min_samp_occur]

## ---- sample metadata (including habitat) ------------------------------------
sdat_dd <- dat_all_filt_combine_prim %>%
  filter(type == "sample") %>%
  distinct(sample_id, lat, lon, habitat) %>%
  filter(sample_id %in% rownames(otu_wide)) %>%
  arrange(match(sample_id, rownames(otu_wide)))

## ---- Through-water distance (km) -------------------------------------------
## Load pre-computed matrix (run through_water_dist chunk once first)
tw_mat   <- as.matrix(read.csv(paste0(dir, "through_water_dist_km.csv"),
                               row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE))
tw_mat   <- tw_mat[sdat_dd$sample_id, sdat_dd$sample_id]
geo_dist <- as.dist(tw_mat)
attr(geo_dist, "Labels") <- sdat_dd$sample_id

## ---- Bray-Curtis dissimilarity ----------------------------------------------
vg <- vegdist(otu_wide, method = "bray", binary = FALSE)

## ---- Build pairwise data frame with habitat labels --------------------------
pairs_df <- dist2df(geo_dist) %>%
  rename(sample1 = row, sample2 = col, km = value) %>%
  left_join(select(sdat_dd, sample_id, habitat), by = c("sample1" = "sample_id")) %>%
  rename(hab1 = habitat) %>%
  left_join(select(sdat_dd, sample_id, habitat), by = c("sample2" = "sample_id")) %>%
  rename(hab2 = habitat) %>%
  mutate(bc        = as.vector(vg),
         within_hab = if_else(hab1 == hab2, hab1, NA_character_),
         hab_pair   = if_else(hab1 == hab2, hab1, "Between habitats"))

## ---- Compute loess fits per habitat with 95% CI ----------------------------
loess_fits <- pairs_df %>%
  filter(!is.na(within_hab), is.finite(km)) %>%
  group_by(within_hab) %>%
  group_modify(~{
    fit    <- loess(bc ~ km, data = .x, span = 0.75)
    km_seq <- seq(min(.x$km), max(.x$km), length.out = 300)
    pred   <- predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(km = km_seq), se = TRUE)
    data.frame(km  = km_seq,
               fit = pred$fit,
               lwr = pred$fit - 1.96 * pred$se.fit,
               upr = pred$fit + 1.96 * pred$se.fit)
  }) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(within_hab = factor(within_hab, levels = c("Coral", "Mangrove", "Seagrass"))) %>%
  arrange(within_hab)

## ---- Distance-decay plot by habitat -----------------------------------------
p_dd <- ggplot() +
  geom_point(data = filter(pairs_df, !is.na(within_hab), is.finite(km)),
             aes(km, bc, colour = within_hab), alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8) +
  ## Transparent coloured CI ribbon
  geom_ribbon(data = loess_fits,
              aes(x = km, ymin = lwr, ymax = upr, fill = within_hab),
              alpha = 0.22) +
  ## Thin lines on ribbon edges
  geom_line(data = loess_fits,
            aes(x = km, y = lwr, colour = within_hab),
            linewidth = 0.25) +
  geom_line(data = loess_fits,
            aes(x = km, y = upr, colour = within_hab),
            linewidth = 0.25) +
  ## Solid loess line
  geom_line(data = loess_fits,
            aes(x = km, y = fit, colour = within_hab),
            linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = hab_cols, name = "Habitat") +
  scale_fill_manual(values  = hab_cols, name = "Habitat") +
  labs(x = "Through-water distance (km)",
       y = "Bray-Curtis dissimilarity") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "right")

p_dd

ggsave(paste0(dir, plot_file, "/Fig7_dist_decay.tiff"),
       p_dd, width = 14, height = 10, units = "cm", dpi = 300)
```
